Cracker Barrel’s fourth-quarter restaurant sales declined as traffic fell 6.1 percent, but new CEO David Deno sees a path to improvement in the food guests order, the service they receive, and the retail shop they visit on their way out. Deno, who took the job roughly six weeks before the company’s earnings call, said he spent his first weeks visiting stores and speaking with employees and guests. His early assessment places dinner at the top of the list for food investment. Cracker Barrel plans to upgrade its chicken, hamburger, and steak offerings and work on delivering meals that meet guest expectations for taste, temperature, and quality on every visit. READ MORE : Cracker Barrel Names Former Bloomin’ Brands CEO David Deno New Chief Executive Cracker Barrel Sells Maple Street Biscuit Company Assets Why Cracker Barrel is Feeling Confident in its Turnaround The investments are included in the company’s fiscal 2027 outlook. Breakfast continues to produce Cracker Barrel’s strongest food scores and traffic trends, giving the chain a source of strength as it works on dinner. The plan follows a fourth quarter in which comparable restaurant sales fell 2.1 percent. Traffic declined 6.1 percent, offset in part by a 4.2 percent increase in average check that included 4.4 percent pricing. CFO Craig Pommells said comparisons with the prior year varied considerably between the third and fourth quarters. Adjusting for that variability, he described the traffic trend as gradually improving. Fourth-quarter revenue came in above the company’s expectations. Total revenue was $849.3 million, including $698.5 million from restaurants and $150.8 million from retail. Off-premises business accounted for 19 percent of restaurant sales, up roughly one percentage point from a year earlier, driven by third-party delivery growth. Cracker Barrel expects comparable restaurant sales to rise 3 to 5 percent in fiscal 2027, with pricing contributing roughly 3 percent for the full year. It projects total revenue of $3.325 billion to $3.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $180 million to $200 million. The forecast calls for no new restaurants this fiscal year. Pommells said menu changes should contribute alongside pricing. Guests have responded to new appetizers and shareable items, as well as the option to upgrade an entrée from two sides to three. Those purchases offer a way to lift menu margins as the company works to bring more customers into its restaurants. “We do think as we look to the future and we think about dinner and so on, there’s opportunity in the menu mix component of the business that is a win-win for our customers and then obviously improving our margins as well,” Pommells said. Deno said the company will pursue savings in areas guests are less likely to notice, including work outside the restaurants and technology. Inside the stores, he pointed to dessert sales and side orders as opportunities to improve margins through what guests choose to buy. The company also reported gains in several guest measures. Its Google Star rating increased 2 percent year-over-year in the fourth quarter and stayed near an all-time high. Food taste and service scores rose nearly 400 basis points from the year-earlier period, and food temperature scores improved 500 basis points. Hourly employee turnover improved 450 basis points, and manager turnover improved 85 basis points. Deno said training and development will be part of sustaining those gains. Cracker Barrel employs roughly 75,000 people, and he identified store teams as essential to delivering a consistent visit. The retail shop is another opportunity. He brings with him more than 20 years of franchise operations experience, including prior leadership with Papa John’s and Burn Boot Camp, and as COO he has overseen real estate, site selection, construction, and new store openings with a focus on strengthening unit-level economics for franchisees. His move into the President role is part of a broader leadership buildout that also updated Iain Douglas’ role to be Chief Strategy and Brand Officer. The brand also added Stacy Nichols as Controller, Arden McLaughlin as Director of Communications and Franchise Engagement, Dave Dodson as Head of Local Store Marketing & Activation, Rachael Buckley as National Brand Manager and Ed Yancey to lead Franchise Development. “Everything we did in the first half of the year was about giving our owners a stronger business to build on,” said Wylie. “As a franchisee myself, I know consistency in the supply chain and discipline in how we grow matter more than any single opening.” Much of the first half of 2026 went into infrastructure. The company relocated its headquarters to Lexington, Kentucky, along with adding a distribution center to the region to supply its growing East Coast presence and destination locations. The move improves supply consistency in a region where Bad Ass Coffee has concentrated much of its recent development. The brand is actively working to complete a full revamp of its back-office systems, giving franchisees clearer visibility into their own unit-level economics and better tools to manage store performance. Bad Ass Coffee also overhauled its market-by-market approach to development and marketing to concentrate on healthy, net new growth. Bad Ass Coffee has grown to 48 total locations with much of that growth coming from existing franchisees adding stores. The brand now has 10 multi-unit owners, with four more preparing to open a second location. “The clearest signal of where this brand is headed is our existing owners choosing to open their second and third stores,” said Wylie. “That kind of reinvestment comes from experienced operators who know the model, and it is the growth we are building the company around.” Looking ahead, Bad Ass Coffee projects 13 new store openings for the full year, bringing its total to 55 locations by the end of 2026. articles.title: MilkShake Factory to Open in Ridgewood, New Jersey
articles.titleKo: MilkShake Factory to Open in Ridgewood, New Jersey
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . MilkShake Factory, the neighborhood dessert destination known for its handspun milkshakes and small-batch, premium chocolates, will open its newest location in Ridgewood, New Jersey, on Saturday, October 10. Located at 63 E. Ridgewood Ave., Ridgewood, NJ 07450, the new shop will bring the brand’s handcrafted desserts to the heart of the village’s bustling downtown. To celebrate, MilkShake Factory Ridgewood will host a grand opening event on October 10 from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m., featuring a buy one, get one free offer on shakes, sundaes and molten cups, free MilkShake Factory T-shirts for the first 100 guests, a gift basket for the first guest in line, a DJ and giveaways throughout the afternoon. The Ridgewood location is owned and operated by franchisees Penn and Tara Miller-Jones, whose connection to MilkShake Factory began when their son attended the University of Pittsburgh. During visits to see him, the couple became regular visitors to the brand’s Forbes Avenue location and quickly became fans of the concept. Later, when friends and former colleagues became MilkShake Factory franchisees, Penn and Tara began exploring the opportunity to bring a location to their own community. “We’ve loved the MilkShake Factory concept for years, and we’re so excited to now have the opportunity to make it part of Ridgewood,” said Penn Miller-Jones, franchisee of MilkShake Factory Ridgewood. “It’s a brand we genuinely love, and we can’t wait to share it with our friends, neighbors, and the entire community.” “Downtown Ridgewood has such great energy and really brings people together,” added Tara Miller-Jones, franchisee of MilkShake Factory Ridgewood. “Families, students, and neighbors are always walking around, shopping, dining, and spending time downtown, and we think MilkShake Factory will fit right into that experience. We’re looking forward to opening our doors and welcoming everyone in.” A popular destination for residents throughout northern New Jersey, Ridgewood was a natural choice for the Miller-Joneses. Its thriving downtown is home to a wide variety of restaurants and shops and draws significant foot traffic from both the village and surrounding communities. MilkShake Factory’s menu features an assortment of indulgent milkshake flavors, including fan favorites like Chocolate Dipped Strawberry and Campfire S’mores, alongside handcrafted sundaes, molten chocolate cups, and housemade chocolate treats. Every item is made with MilkShake Factory’s signature ice cream, created fresh in-store daily using the Edwards family’s exclusive recipe. MilkShake Factory is more than just a dessert shop; it is a brand built on over a century of family tradition and chocolate-making expertise. Founded in 1914, the company began as a small soda fountain and chocolate shop in Pittsburgh, PA, where generations of chocolatiers crafted premium confections using time-honored techniques and the finest ingredients. What started as a local sweet shop has grown into a beloved dessert destination, seamlessly blending classic craftsmanship with modern indulgences. Today, MilkShake Factory stays true to its roots in chocolate and its heritage as a family-founded brand, while bringing joy to new communities across the country through its growing franchise program. MilkShake Factory Ridgewood is located at 63 E. Ridgewood Ave., Ridgewood, NJ 07450. Guests can contact the store at 201-267-4253. For more information, visit MilkShakeFactory.com. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . McDonald’s now serves more than 70 million customers per day. McDonald’s is preparing its largest menu quality upgrade on record as part of a new companywide strategy designed to win traffic in an industry the chain expects to produce little traffic growth. The company unveiled McDonald’s > Next during its investor day, presenting a multiyear plan built around menu improvements, personalized marketing, redesigned restaurants, artificial intelligence, and employee training. The goal is to make McDonald’s the first choice for more customers and improve restaurant productivity enough to fund continued investment. McDonald’s expects industry traffic across its wholly owned markets to stay flat, making market-share gains a greater source of future growth. CEO Chris Kempczinski said companies will have to create demand and serve it with greater efficiency. “The winners will be the companies that create more demand and deliver it more efficiently,” Kempczinski said. READ MORE : McDonald’s Plans $8.5 Billion in Franchisee Support Under New Growth Strategy The strategy follows Accelerating the Arches, which McDonald’s introduced in 2020. Since then, core menu sales have increased more than 50 percent, mobile orders have reached roughly 40 percent of systemwide sales, and the company has added more than 6,000 restaurants. McDonald’s now serves more than 70 million customers per day and counts nearly 220 million regular app and loyalty users. Its global estate exceeds 46,000 restaurants, with a long-term target of 50,000. Menu > Next concentrates on beef, chicken, and beverages. Those categories account for most of McDonald’s business and offer different growth opportunities. The company holds more than 40 percent share of a roughly $50 billion beef category across its 10 largest markets. Its share sits in the high teens for chicken, a nearly $130 billion segment growing more than 5 percent annually. McDonald’s holds high-single-digit share in beverages, a category valued near $230 billion. The chain is targeting roughly 1.5 percentage points of share growth in chicken and beverages by 2030, along with continued dominance in beef. Its chicken plan includes adjusted cooking procedures, expanded McNuggets flavors and sauces, additional McCrispy sandwiches, McWings in more markets, and grilled chicken sandwiches and wraps. McDonald’s is also testing hand-breaded chicken after building expertise across 10,000 restaurants in Asia. Tests will expand to more U.S. and Ireland restaurants with advertising support in 2027. Chicken McNuggets account for nearly $15 billion in annual systemwide sales. McCrispy produces more than $2.5 billion, and McChicken contributes nearly $4 billion. Beverages have become a distinct traffic opportunity following lessons from CosMc’s and market tests. New specialty drinks are available in nearly 18,000 restaurants. More than half of beverage visits occur after lunch, when stores have unused capacity, and checks are roughly 50 percent higher when customers add food to their drinks. “Beverages are no longer just an add-on but a reason to visit,” global chief restaurant experience officer Jill McDonald said. The platform will move into most European markets during the first half of 2027 and reach additional international developmental licensee markets throughout that year. McDonald’s is also improving coffee with fresher beans, new recipes, updated equipment and more customization. Beef initiatives include tighter cooking procedures, dedicated training and possible expansion of fresh Quarter Pounder patties and hot-off-the-grill preparation into more countries. The chain is studying flexible portion options such as burger bowls and plans to extend the Quarter Pounder, Double Quarter Pounder, and Big Arch platforms. articles.title: Pizza Guys Signs Lease in Fort Worth, Texas
articles.titleKo: Pizza Guys Signs Lease in Fort Worth, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Pizza Guys, a Sacramento-based pizza franchise known for fresh, high-quality ingredients, announced today that it has signed a lease for its upcoming Fort Worth restaurant at 3529 Heritage Trace Pkwy, Ste 119. Owned and operated by business partners Kapil Pantha and Tara Rai, the new location marks Pizza Guys’ second restaurant in Texas. This expansion builds on the brand’s successful Texas debut in Plano last year. The Fort Worth location is expected to open early 2027. Pantha and Rai plan to hire a team of at least five employees to support day-to-day operations. Pantha and Rai are more than business partners. In fact, they are close friends and neighbors whose families share deep ties, including a common heritage in Nepal and children who attend the same school. That personal bond, paired with a shared belief in community-focused business, is what drew them to Pizza Guys. “Kapil and Tara bring exactly the kind of partnership and community spirit that makes a Pizza Guys location thrive,” said Shahpour Nejad, CEO and Founder of Pizza Guys . “From our very first conversations with them, it was clear how much they valued the guidance and support our team offers, and that same care is exactly what they’ll bring to Fort Worth. We’re proud to welcome them into the Pizza Guys family as we continue to grow across Texas.” A Partnership Rooted in Community Pantha brings a diverse professional background to his new venture, having started his career in the restaurant industry before managing 7-Eleven convenience stores and later moving into operations for a trucking company. Most recently, he worked in logistics. Rai’s experience includes roles in the restaurant and fast-food sectors alongside a career in the tech sector. Together, the pair believe their combined backgrounds in customer-facing roles and operations position them well for franchise success. “From the moment we met the Pizza Guys team, we knew this was the right fit,” said Pantha . “They walked us through every step of the process. Compared to other food franchises, the lower startup cost made this an opportunity we could realistically pursue. After trying the food ourselves at the Plano location, we knew immediately this was a brand worth investing in.” Being among the first two franchisees bringing Pizza Guys to Texas, Pantha and Rai are deeply committed to establishing a strong foundation for the brand. The Fort Worth restaurant marks the beginning of their journey toward a multi-unit operation. “For us, this is about more than opening a restaurant, it’s about being an active part of the community we live in,” said Rai . “Great customer service, a high-quality product and a welcoming space are what we believe keep guests coming back. We want families to feel right at home when they walk through our doors, the same way we feel at home here in Fort Worth.” The Fort Worth lease signing builds on strong momentum for Pizza Guys, which expanded to more than 100 locations systemwide and celebrated its 40 th anniversary in 2026. The brand continues to prioritize thoughtful growth, strong franchisee support, and quality service across California, Nevada, and Texas. To learn more about Pizza Guys or view the menu, visit pizzaguys.com. For information on franchise opportunities, visit pizzaguys.com/franchise-opportunities. Mo’ Bettahs Hawaiian Style Food is growing its presence in Utah with a new restaurant opening Sept. 25 at 10969 N. Town Center in Highland. The opening marks the brand’s 36 th restaurant in the state where its story began nearly two decades ago. Founded in nearby Bountiful in 2008, Mo’ Bettahs was built on the recipes, traditions and hospitality brothers Kimo and Kalani Mack grew up with on O‘ahu. The brand serves Hawaiian-style plate lunches featuring favorites like teriyaki chicken and steak, kalua pig, pulehu chicken and katsu chicken, paired with steamed rice, vegetables and creamy macaroni salad. Ahead of the grand opening, Mo’ Bettahs will celebrate with the Highland community during a Friends and ʻOhana event Sept. 24, bringing the spirit of a Hawaiian hoʻolauleʻa to the neighborhood. The event is open to the public, beginning with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at 4:30 p.m., followed by complimentary mini plates and drinks from 5 to 7 p.m. featuring samples and merchandise (while supplies last). “Utah will always be a special place for Mo’ Bettahs because it’s where Kimo and I first had the chance to share the food and traditions we grew up with,” said Kalani Mack, co-founder of Mo’ Bettahs. “Nearly 20 years later, it means a lot to continue growing here and welcoming new communities like Highland into our ʻohana. We look forward to gathering around the table with our new neighbors and sharing a little Aloha.” The Highland location will be the newest stop on Mo’ Bettahs’ growing map of communities across the country, marking the brand’s 83rd location nationwide. The opening continues the brand’s corporate-led expansion into new and existing markets. The restaurant will be open Monday through Saturday from 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. and closed Sundays. Guests can dine in, order takeout or explore catering options . To learn more, view the full menu or place an order, visit mobettahs.com. Prince St. Pizza, the New York City-born pizzeria known for its Sicilian-style square pies and signature pepperoni-loaded slices, is joining forces with Megadeth on a limited-edition pizza created in celebration of the 40th Anniversary of the release of the band’s Platinum album, Peace Sells…But Who’s Buying. Available Sept. 23 through Sept. 27 at Los Angeles locations, the collaboration will also give fans a chance to attend sold-out, An Evening with Megadeth at the Grammy Museum on Sept. 24 and meet the band. Megadeth formed in 1983 by Dave Mustaine and spent the next four decades shaping what heavy metal sounds like. Fifty million records, a Grammy Award, 12 more nominations and nine Top 10 entries on the Billboard 200 later, the band still plays loud and fast for millions of global fans. They are currently on the sold out Run For Your Lives stadium tour with Iron Maiden. The Vic’s Pepperoni is a New York-style round built on original pizza sauce, shredded mozzarella and all-beef pepperoni; packaged in a custom box designed for this promotion. “Megadeth and Prince St. Pizza come from different worlds, but there’s a real connection in the way both brands have built loyal followings by staying authentic to who they are,” said Lawrence Longo, CEO of Prince St. Pizza. “For us, this partnership is about bringing those two worlds together in a way that feels genuine, unexpected and fun for the fans who have helped us become what we are today.” With the show currently sold out, the pizza also becomes another way in. Rewards members who order a slice or a full-size Vic’s Pepperoni are entered to win one of five pairs, 10 seats in total, to the Sept. 24 performance. Entries close Sept. 23 at 8 p.m. No purchase is necessary to enter or win, and fans may also enter via e-mail in accordance with the official rules. One of the five winners will also receive the grand prize of sitting down with Mustaine, Teemu Mäntysaari, James LoMenzo and Dirk Verbeuren to enjoy a slice of pizza before the show on Sept. 24. Another 20 will take home a collaboration box signed by Megadeth, packed with a Peace Sells T-shirt. Founded in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood over a decade ago, Prince St. Pizza has become a national destination for its crave-worthy square pies, now served at 20 locations across the U.S. and Canada. FONDUE INTO FALL Available for a limited time at participating restaurants, the three-course Fondue Into Fall experience features: Cranberry Pecan Cheese Fondue: Butterkäse and Fontina blended with apple cider, Cherrywood smoked ham, dried cranberries, candied pecans and scallions, served with artisan breads, fresh fruit and vegetables. We are proud to help mark Family Feud’s 50th anniversary by bringing the excitement of the game directly into our restaurants.” “As Family Feud celebrates 50 years on television, we’re excited to partner with TGI Fridays to bring thegame show experience beyond the screen,” said Jennifer Mullin, CEO, Fremantle. “With gameplay available at participating TGI Fridays locations, fans can enjoy the fun, laughter and friendly competition they’ve come to expect from Family Feud while sharing a great meal with family and friends.” “Today’s guests are looking for more than just a meal. They want memorable experiences they can enjoy and share together,” said Misty Shannon, Senior Director of Marketing at TGI Fridays. “This partnership brings together great food, friendly competition and interactive entertainment in a way that feels uniquely TGI Fridays. Whether guests are stopping in for dinner, celebrating a special occasion or just gathering with friends, Family Feud adds another reason to stay, play and connect.” Guests can pair the experience with both beloved Fridays® classics and new menu additions like Mike’s Hot Honey Chicken Sliders, Shrimp Scampi Pasta and Tostado Nachos introduced this fall, giving friends and families even more reasons to gather, share and celebrate. The partnership combines two brands built around bringing people together, transforming a traditional dining occasion into an interactive experience centered on friendly competition, conversation and connection. Originally premiering in July 1976, Family Feud became one of the highest-rated game shows on daytime television. Five decades later, it remains a powerhouse in syndication, averaging 7.5 million daily viewers during the 2025–2026 season. Hosted by Emmy Award-winning television personality and best-selling author Steve Harvey, new episodes of Family Feud begin September 28, 2026. Availability and participation may vary by location. For more information, visit http://www.tgifridays.com/ or download the new TGI Fridays app for free on the App Store and Google Play to find your nearest location, place an order and manage rewards. articles.title: The Cumberland Backs Hart Hambleton Growth with New Funding
articles.titleKo: The Cumberland Backs Hart Hambleton Growth with New Funding
articles.originalSummary: The Cumberland Building Society has strengthened its support for an established UK country house hotel – along with its fast-growing bakery arm—by providing a refinancing package designed to fuel the next phase of expansion. The society has provided new funding to Hart Hambleton, the Rutland‑based hospitality and food‑and‑drink group behind the business, enabling it to build on its recent momentum and pursue further growth opportunities. Supporting the group’s Hambleton Hall and Hambleton Bakery businesses, the funding builds on The Cumberland’s strong track record in aiding both hospitality organisations and businesses in the food and drinks sector. Owned by Tim Hart, Hart Hambleton has been a part of the region’s hospitality and food and drink offering for more than four decades, attracting guests from across the UK and abroad, as well as holding a strong following of local customers. The group encompasses Hambleton Hall, a Grade II Listed country house hotel, Hambleton Bakery, a food and drink business with eight shops and a cafe, and Hart’s Hotel and Kitchen. Tim established Hambleton Hall in 1980, growing it into a successful business whose restaurant has held a Michelin star since 1982 and regularly features among the top ten country house hotels in the UK, according to The Times and The Telegraph. Alongside the hotel, the Hambleton Bakery has grown into a significant food operation since it was established in 2008, headed up by Julian Carter who worked as a chef in Hambleton Hall. The bakery now manufactures and distributes its own produce, supplying over 200 independent retailers, restaurants and cafes on a wholesale basis, while serving customers directly through its eight owned retail shops and cafe. It has been recognised nationally, being featured in ITV’s Britain’s Best Bakery and Wild About Food in 2012, which is still remembered by visitors today. While successful, Hart Hambleton looked to refinance the hotel and bakery businesses’ lending in a bid to maintain operations while opening up opportunities for future growth. Being introduced to The Cumberland by broker Zain Zaidi of Enness Global, the society’s Commercial team worked to understand the needs of both Hambleton Hall and Hambleton Bakery. As a result, the society’s dedicated Relationship Manager was able to develop a refinancing solution which met the ambition of the group. Tim Hart, Owner of Hart Hambleton, said: “The Cumberland understood what we have built here and what we are trying to achieve. This is not a straightforward business and having a lender with expertise across both hospitality and food and drink sectors made a real difference. “They took the time to understand the group properly, not just the numbers, but the ethos behind what we have built over the years. That level of understanding is increasingly rare, and it gave us confidence from the outset that we were working with the right partner. “The refinancing gives us a strong foundation and the breathing room to focus on what we do best, running exceptional businesses and looking after the people who make them what they are.” With more than 30 years’ experience dedicated to providing commercial lending to hospitality businesses, The Cumberland also supports organisations across the food and drink sector, offering services including commercial mortgages, current accounts and savings accounts. Every commercial mortgage customer is supported by a dedicated Relationship Manager, providing tailored guidance and consistent support throughout the lending process and beyond.
koreanSummary: The Cumberland Building Society has strengthened its support for an established UK country house hotel – along with its fast-growing bakery arm—by providing a refinancing package designed to fuel the next phase of expansion.

The society has provided new funding to Hart Hambleton, the Rutland‑based hospitality and food‑and‑drink group behind the business, enabling it to build on its recent momentum and pursue further growth opportunities.

Supporting the group’s Hambleton Hall and Hambleton Bakery businesses, the funding builds on The Cumberland’s strong track record in aiding both hospitality organisations and businesses in the food and drinks sector.

articles.title: Delamere Launches 97ml Oat Drink for Hospotality Industry
articles.titleKo: Delamere Launches 97ml Oat Drink for Hospotality Industry
articles.originalSummary: Delamere has announced the launch of a new 97ml oat drink following the success of its semi-skimmed milk mini bottles in the hospitality and foodservice industries. Designed for hospitality settings, such as hotel room trays, breakfast buffets and on-board catering, the bottles can be used to add to hot drinks or pour over cereal. The oat drink has been developed to offer a plant-based alternative to cows’ milk, enabling accommodation and foodservice providers to cater to different dietary requirements and evolving consumer preferences. The ambient product has a shelf life of up to six months and once opened, it can be treated as fresh milk and stored in the fridge. Each bottle contains 3-4 servings and can be re-closed and stored by guests, eliminating the single-use plastic associated with milk pots and sticks and saving time on repeat deliveries of fresh milk to rooms. The premium glass bottles, capped with an aluminium lid, are fully recyclable, supporting outlets in implementing responsible waste management practices. Available now, the new oat drink can be purchased directly through Brakes and via wholesalers nationwide. Dan Yates, national account manager at Delamere, said: “Our mini milk bottles are already a trusted choice in hotels and hospitality settings, so the creation of a plant-based oat drink in the same format felt like the natural next step when adding to the range. “Sustainable, premium and convenient, we’re confident that it will soon be a staple part of the guest experience.” Located in Knutsford, Cheshire, Delamere has been producing award-winning dairy products for more than 40 years. It supplies an extensive range of speciality goat and cows’ milk based products to retail, wholesale and independent customers across the UK and in over 20 markets around the world.

articles.title: Does Your Holiday Menu Actually Make Money?
articles.titleKo: Does Your Holiday Menu Actually Make Money?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Too many restaurants ask, "What sounds fun?" The better question is, "What can we execute perfectly on our busiest nights?" A holiday menu should never be built around excitement. It should be built around profitability and execution. If your kitchen can’t consistently execute it during the busiest season of the year, it doesn’t matter how creative it is. Keep reading to learn how to build a holiday menu that actually makes you money, not the most exciting one. Getting your restaurant menu pricing right is where that difference shows up. Start with the menu’s purpose, not the excitement When I coach restaurant owners on developing a holiday menu that will make money, I start with first principles. A holiday menu’s job isn’t to prove your chef is creative or show off seasonal ingredients. Its job is to increase sales, protect profitability, deliver a great guest experience and make life easier for your team. If it does all four, you’ve won. Too many restaurants ask, “What sounds fun?” The better question is, “What can we execute perfectly on our busiest nights?” Every new item you put on the menu adds new ingredients, prep, training and chances for mistakes. Picture your kitchen on a Friday night in December, every table full, tickets stacked. That’s not the moment to lean on recipes your cooks have only made twice. Hope is not a strategy. Execution is. Use what you already have for your holiday menu One of the fastest ways to destroy holiday profits is buying ingredients you’ll only use in one dish, then throwing the leftovers away in January. Instead, build dishes around ingredients you already buy. Can the same mushroom work in three menu items? Can that seasonal sauce work with chicken, pasta and steak? Every ingredient should earn its place in the walk-in. The restaurants that make the most money during the holidays aren’t buying the most ingredients; they’re using their ingredients more intelligently. Price your holiday menu for value, not fear This is where restaurant owners get nervous about restaurant menu pricing. They worry about charging too much. Instead, ask what a guest is really buying when they’ve already decided to celebrate at your restaurant. They’re buying memories, atmosphere and celebration, not the cheapest plate in town. Stop pricing from fear. Price your menu based on value, and understand what each plate contributes toward labor, rent, utilities and profit. Food cost percentages matter, but contribution matters more. A dish with a slightly higher food cost may still make you more money if it delivers more dollars to your bottom line. Don’t confuse percentages with profit. Protect your portions and your prep Holiday volume exposes every weakness in your operation. If one cook serves 6 ounces, another serves 8 and another serves 10, your food cost isn’t rising because of inflation. It’s rising because your standards disappeared. Every recipe needs exact portions, and every garnish and protein needs a set size. Guessing gets expensive. Consistency makes money. This is also where recipe costing becomes non-negotiable. Too many restaurants create a holiday special before they know what it costs. Every recipe should be fully costed before it reaches your menu, because once it’s printed, your restaurant menu pricing decisions are locked in. Know your numbers first, then decide your price. Watch for bottlenecks Ask where a dish creates bottlenecks. Does it tie up the grill or the fryer? Does it need one person who knows a complicated finishing process? During slow periods, that’s fine. During December, a few extra minutes becomes longer ticket times, frustrated guests, and refunds and bad reviews. The best holiday menu is often the simplest one. articles.title: Shula’s Restaurant Group Announces Dave Shula as President
articles.titleKo: Shula’s Restaurant Group Announces Dave Shula as President
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Shula’s Restaurant Group announces Dave Shula as President, returning the longtime company leader to the role as the restaurant group enters its next phase of growth. Shula, the eldest son of Pro Football Hall of Fame Coach Don Shula, previously served as president for nearly 20 years and will lead the organization as it expands its six-concept portfolio nationwide. Under his leadership, the company will focus on supporting growth across its existing franchise concepts while pursuing new opportunities, including the opening of Shula’s American Kitchen at the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel and Executive Meeting Center Palm Beach Gardens this winter. Expansion plans also include entry into Thomasville, Georgia, a new market for the brand, in 2027, with additional opportunities under exploration nationwide. As president, he will also lead team building and development within the corporate organization, while working to reinforce the Shula culture across the company’s restaurant portfolio. “My family name is on this organization and each of our franchised locations, so it’s important to me as an owner that the company reflects the goals my dad laid out for me when I first joined in 1997,” Shula said. “He told me, ‘I didn’t get into the restaurant business to do anything but enhance the reputation I built as a football coach.’ That sets the bar high and continues to guide how we operate today.” Shula’s leadership approach draws from the principles that defined his father’s career: preparation, discipline, accountability, teamwork and integrity. Coach Don Shula led the Miami Dolphins to the only perfect season in NFL history, finishing 17-0 in 1972, a feat no other team has matched in the NFL’s 105-year history. Shula’s Steak House was founded in 1989 to bring those same standards to hospitality and has since grown into a restaurant group with six concepts and more than 30 locations nationwide over the last 37 years. Before entering hospitality, Shula played for the Baltimore Colts in 1981 and began his coaching career with the Miami Dolphins under his father in 1982. He later served as Offensive Coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys before serving as Head Coach of the Cincinnati Bengals from 1992 to 1996. Following his NFL coaching career, he joined the family restaurant business in 1997 and spent more than two decades helping lead its growth and development as President and National Ambassador, Shula returned to football in 2018 as Wide Receivers coach at Dartmouth College, his alma mater, where he coached through 2023. Outside the company, Shula has served on the Orange Bowl Committee since 2016 and was named vice mayor of Jupiter Inlet Colony earlier this year. A lifelong athlete, he has completed four full Ironman events and several half Ironman races over 25 years of triathlon competition. He and his wife, Leslie, married 44 years after meeting as student-athletes at Dartmouth, enjoy spending time with their three sons and six grandchildren. For more information on Shula’s Restaurant Group, visit shulas.com or follow on Instagram at @shulasrestaurantgroup. For franchise development opportunities, visit shulas.com/franchise. articles.title: Ninety Nine Restaurants Could Be Headed for a Sale
articles.titleKo: Ninety Nine Restaurants Could Be Headed for a Sale
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ninety Nine operates 93 company-owned restaurants across seven northeastern states. Ninety Nine Restaurant & Pub could be headed for a change in ownership as Cannae Holdings reviews its restaurant business, according to The Boston Globe . Cannae has been weighing strategic alternatives for its two remaining restaurant chains, Ninety Nine and O’Charley’s. The latter abruptly closed company-owned restaurants across the country on September 9 . The Globe reported that Cannae CEO Ryan Caswell has indicated the company expects proceeds from a sale, though no transaction involving Ninety Nine has been announced. The possible sale comes at a markedly different point for the two sister brands. Ninety Nine operates 93 company-owned restaurants across seven northeastern states, according to Cannae’s first-quarter shareholder letter. Cannae said the chain remained profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis during the quarter, while O’Charley’s continued to struggle to retain customers and bring in new ones. Ninety Nine’s same-store sales fell about 3 percent in the first half of 2026, compared with a decline of about 13 percent at O’Charley’s, the Globe reported. O’Charley’s closures unfolded with little warning to employees. Workers at restaurants in Tennessee, Illinois and Kentucky told local news outlets they had been informed that their locations would close permanently at 8 p.m. September 9. Some said they received one day’s notice or learned of the decision that morning. The closures brought a sharp end to company-owned operations at a chain that once had nearly 250 restaurants nationwide. A franchised restaurant in Niles, Ohio, was expected to remain open until September 27. Ninety Nine has sought to distance its operations from those closures. A spokesperson told the Globe that decisions involving O’Charley’s would have no impact on Ninety Nine and said the chain would continue serving its New England guests regardless of any ownership change. Founded by Charlie Doe in Boston in 1952, Ninety Nine takes its name from the address of its first restaurant, 99 State Street. The Doe family sold the regional chain to O’Charley’s in 2002. Today, it remains concentrated in the Northeast, with more than 4,000 employees, according to the Globe. The post Ninety Nine Restaurants Could Be Headed for a Sale appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Starbird Chicken Growing in Washington with Mehta Investment Group

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Starbird Chicken, the award-winning fast casual chicken concept known for its fresh, globally inspired flavors, is expanding its footprint into Washington through a new franchise partnership with Mehta Investment Group . The agreement includes plans to develop 17 locations across Washington state. The expansion marks a significant step in Starbird’s continued growth as the company brings its signature chicken tenders, salads, and sandwiches to new guests throughout the Pacific Northwest. The new franchise venture will be led by Vin Mehta and his son Rohit through Mehta Investment Group, a family-owned enterprise with experience across multiple industries and a strong track record of building successful operations. Vin Mehta, president of Mehta Investment Group, will guide the strategic direction of the restaurants, while Rohit Mehta will oversee day-to-day operations and support the brand’s growth throughout Washington. “Starbird has built something truly special by reimagining what a chicken restaurant can be, from the bold flavors and hospitable, modern restaurant design to the overall guest experience,” said Mehta. “Together, we’ll combine Starbird’s innovative approach with our team’s operational experience and passion for building lasting connections. We’re excited to open in Washington and become part of the communities we serve.” The Washington expansion builds on the brand’s momentum as the company continues to grow through both company owned and strategic franchise partnerships in new markets. With Mehta Investment Group’s operational expertise and commitment to community-focused restaurants, Starbird will continue bringing its signature approach to chicken to more guests nationwide. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mendocino Farms, the celebrated Southern California-born fast-casual restaurant chain known for turning sandwiches, salads, and chef-driven catering into an unexpected culinary adventure, continues its Texas growth with the opening of its third Austin location at 1100 South Lamar Boulevard, Suite 1125, Austin, Texas 78704, on Tuesday, September 22. The opening follows strong debuts at Arbor Trails and West 38th Street, and adds to a Texas footprint that has grown to 14 restaurants statewide. This marks location number 102 nationwide, with more on the way. Mendocino Farms continues to elevate the local fast-casual scene, pairing high-quality ingredients with bold flavors and signature hospitality. As the brand’s third Austin destination, guests can enjoy beloved staples like the “Not So Fried” Chicken Sandwich, The Farm Club, and the Happy Hippie, alongside seasonal standouts such as the charred Fajita Steak Salad and the returning fan-favorite Seasonal GOAT Salad with Pink Lady Apples. “Ever since we opened our first Austin location in 2025, the community has embraced Mendocino Farms and showed us incredible support. Opening our third location is an exciting milestone that truly reflects that continued support,” said Alicia Mowder, Chief Marketing Officer of Mendocino Farms. “As we continue to grow in the Austin area, we’re committed to bringing even more people craft sandwiches and salads and warm hospitality that we’re known for.” To celebrate the Grand Opening, guests who sign up for a Mendocino Farms eClub Account and select South Lamar as their favorite location prior to Grand Opening Day will receive a free entrée with any purchase, loaded directly into their account on Opening Day and valid for two weeks. Guests may continue to join the eClub after this date to receive future perks and offers. The opening of the new South Lamar location will also kick off the brand’s ongoing giveback program. Through the end of December, Mendocino Farms South Lamar will offer local schools, nonprofits, and community organizations the opportunity to host in-store fundraiser events and receive 50 percent back on all qualifying purchases, helping the community raise funds and bringing people together to Eat Happy. For guests interested in finding out more about the giveback program, they can visit http://mendocinofarms.force4good.com . His background in Korean and French fine-dining kitchens shapes how he cooks today, bringing Korean flavors together with Texas ingredients and premium beef. For Kim, that point of view is also personal. His connection to Korean cuisine began with the food he grew up eating with his grandparents, particularly homemade kimchi, and the simplicity and care that went into preparing it. Those early experiences continue to influence how he thinks about food today: less about strict recreations and more about preserving the flavors, memories and sense of generosity that gave those dishes meaning. “In Korean culture, sharing food is how we connect,” said Kim. “I want guests to feel that at Nuri and have an approachable way to experience Korean food, even if the flavors are new to them.” Nuri owner Wan Kim said the appointment reflects the restaurant’s continued evolution and its original vision of bringing cultures together around the steakhouse format. “Nuri was created to bring people and cultures together around the table,” said owner Wan Kim. “This next chapter gives that vision a clearer Korean point of view. Mike's Red Tacos has sold 350 franchise commitments. Three-unit Mike’s Red Tacos did not begin with a sweeping national plan. It started with a food trend, a friendship, and a suggestion to think bigger. CEO Andrew Feghali had known founder Mike Touma for roughly a decade when Touma approached him with an observation. Birria was gaining traction, and he believed the Mexican specialty could follow a path similar to hot chicken. Feghali brought experience from a franchise portfolio of roughly 100 restaurants across Little Caesars, Jersey Mike’s, and Dave’s Hot Chicken, where he was the first franchisee. The pair spent several weeks visiting birria concepts and sampling the food. Touma initially envisioned selling birria tacos from a trailer stationed outside one of his retail shops. Feghali saw room for a full restaurant. “I said, OK, I think that’s cool. I think you should think a little bit bigger, and open a restaurant. I think you’re onto something interesting here,” Feghali says. Touma later asked Feghali to become his partner. They leased a food truck, and Touma developed the brand, selling tacos on Saturdays in a friend’s parking lot beginning at 11 a.m. and continuing until the food ran out. He eventually opened the first brick-and-mortar restaurant, which landed on Yelp’s list of the top 100 restaurants in the U.S. within a few months. That early recognition offered proof that the concept could attract diners outside its initial following. It also gave the partners a foundation for turning a single restaurant into a franchise opportunity. Feghali then organized the investment group behind the franchise platform, called Four Wall Partners. The idea gained traction faster than its partners anticipated. The company has sold roughly 350 franchise commitments and has several hundred more in its pipeline, Feghali says. That acceleration changed his role. Feghali had been an active board member offering strategic guidance to the corporate team. As the company added employees and awarded large territories, partner and mentor Bill Phelps encouraged him to become CEO. Feghali was initially reluctant. He was content serving as an investor and board member. Conversations with Phelps changed his perspective. He came to see the position as a way to serve the company’s stakeholders and advance Four Wall Partners’ mission of transforming lives across its franchise systems. With close friends joining the corporate team and becoming franchisees, Feghali felt responsible for giving the brand its best chance to succeed and honoring the trust placed in him. The personal stakes were clear. Touma was a longtime family friend who trusted Feghali to assemble the deal, and new hires had left good jobs or declined other opportunities to join the company. “The executive team are folks that have come on board that have left great jobs or passed on other great opportunities because in large part they trusted me,” Feghali says. Operators signed because of the food, category, and business model, he says, but personal trust also influenced their decisions. Taking the CEO job became a way to honor the people committing careers and capital to the venture. “I really feel like it’s more of a service role than something that I had wanted,” Feghali says. “I didn’t have aspirations of becoming CEO of an emerging franchise brand.” Mike’s has its own identity and origin story, though Feghali acknowledges parallels with Dave’s. Each specializes in a segment of a much larger category. Dave’s helped propel Nashville hot chicken into the national conversation. Mike’s sees similar potential for birria within fast-casual Mexican. Feghali says consumer awareness and menu penetration for birria are tracking on a trajectory similar to hot chicken several years ago. articles.title: For Yum! Brands, Life After Pizza Hut Starts with an ‘Acceleration of Growth’

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The fact Yum! Brands divested Pizza Hut earlier this month , splitting the chain from KFC for the first time in nearly four decades, should signal the company is prepared to make bold moves, CFO Ranjith Roy said. Could that include adding another concept to accompany the chicken giant, Taco Bell, and fast casual Habit Burger & Grill? Sure, if it makes sense, Roy shared at the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “We’re open to the idea,” he said. But meanwhile, Yum! feels it has plenty to occupy its calendar with what’s already here. Roy said portfolio discipline sits atop the company’s near-term targets. And if you examine the number of opportunities ahead, “we could spend all day right now accelerating growth at KFC, Taco Bell, and Habit, and we wouldn’t have much time to spare,” he explained. Roy noted 2027 will be an “extraordinarily exciting year” for Yum! Brands as investors and competitors get their first clean look at life post-Pizza Hut, which comprised about 10–12 percent of its operating profit. Naturally, though, Pizza Hut took ample time, resources, and focus to manage a 15,500-unit system generating $10 billion in annual systemwide sales. The sale came after several years of declining domestic performance and shrinking units counts. In Q1, U.S. same-store sales slid 4 percent and systemwide figures 6 percent. Across fiscal 2025, Pizza Hut’s comps declined 5 percent and systemwide 8 percent on top of another calendar of red performance in 2024. Pizza Hut finished the period with 6,121 U.S. restaurants, down from 6,551 five years earlier. Yum! agreed to deal the 1958-founded chain—excluding Mainland China—for $1.5 billion to LongRange Capital. Yum! China assumed control of the other part for $1.2 billion. It marked the first time in 54 years Pizza Hut was private. It was 14 years old in 1972 when it began trading. Atari released Pong that year. More largely, Yum!’s roots track to 1977 when PepsiCo was a decade into plans to diversify beyond beverages after merging with Frito-Lay. It bought Pizza Hut and, a year later, tacked on Taco Bell. KFC joined in 1986. Yum! materialized in 2002 following PepsiCo’s 1997 shift toward drinks and snacks and the decision to spin-off its brands into Tricon Global Restaurants. Long John Silver’s and A&W arrived five years later and Yum! was created (those latter two were sold in 2011 and Habit acquired in 2020). History aside, though, Roy said Pizza Hut exiting the portfolio means Yum! can divert its energy into an “acceleration of growth.” CEO Chris Turner, who elevated to the role about a year ago (October), succeeding 37-year company veteran David Gibbs, has been out talking about raising the bar, Roy said. That includes the battle for the future consumer, propelling unit economics, and expanding the reach of Yum!’s proprietary tech platform, Byte, which was introduced in February 2025 as an online and mobile app ordering, point of sale, kitchen and delivery optimization, menu management, inventory and labor management, and employee tool unifier across the system. “There’s a number of work streams underway at the company right now that will start to play out over the course of the rest of this year and 2027,” Roy said. “And just the freedom to be able to pursue them with more focus, having a more concentrated portfolio is very exciting.” So, regarding the notion of buying another chain, the lead focus for Yum! will first be asking, has it raised the performance of its existing brands? Even sans Pizza Hut, it’s a portfolio spanning 34,747 KFCs (Q2 close), 9,046 Taco Bells, and 388 Habits. “Our first priority is investing in our current businesses,” Roy said. “We’ll continue to do that. articles.title: Katz’s Deli Adds First New Soda in Decades
articles.titleKo: Katz’s Deli Adds First New Soda in Decades
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Katz’s Delicatessen is breaking a decades-long streak and Ben Stiller is to blame. For the first time in decades, the iconic Lower East Side deli is adding a new soda to its menu: Stiller’s Soda. The partnership marks a new collaboration between two quintessential New York institutions, bringing Stiller’s nostalgic, NYC-inspired sodas to the home of legendary hand-carved pastrami and corned beef. The collaboration marks a first in Katz’s storied history: a Shirley Temple is officially joining the menu. Inspired by Stiller’s lifelong love of classic soda and his New York City upbringing, the Shirley Temple joins Stiller’s Soda’s lineup of nostalgic favorites, including Shirley Cola, Root Beer and Lemon Lime. At Katz’s, the new soda offering provides a playful counterpoint to one of the city’s most iconic deli experiences. “This is a really special partnership for Stiller’s,” said Alex Doman, the slightly less famous Co-Founder and CEO of Stiller’s Soda. “Katz’s is a New York institution and part of the fabric of the city. Seeing Stiller’s alongside its famous pastrami and corned beef is a pretty incredible moment for us. We’re a New York-born brand inspired by the joy and nostalgia of classic soda, so partnering with a place with this much history feels like a perfect fit.” Founded in 1888, Katz’s Delicatessen has been a New York City institution for generations, known for its traditional Jewish deli fare, house-cured meats and legendary hand-carved sandwiches. The partnership with Stiller’s Soda brings together Katz’s enduring New York legacy with a brand built around the nostalgia and fun of classic soda. To celebrate the partnership, Stiller teamed up with New York City creator New York Nico for a new social video that takes the announcement in a decidedly unexpected direction, now live on YouTube and Instagram. In the video, Stiller arrives at Katz’s, fully convinced he is there to film Cats the musical, not a soda commercial. He commits to the bit so completely that he arrives dressed as Munkustrap, the character from the Broadway production. The costume was created by Sarah Edwards, Stiller’s costume designer from the Apple TV+ show, Severance , who tapped friends connected to the original Broadway production to help source the look, including one of the production’s original wigs. The result is Stiller, in full Munkustrap costume, arriving at Katz’s to introduce Stiller’s Soda and the deli’s newest Shirley Temple menu addition. Keep up with the latest from Stiller’s Soda by following @StillersSoda on social media or visit www.stillerssoda.com for more info. Hilton McLean Tysons Corner is pleased to announce the appointment of Daniel Sosa as director of culinary. In this elevated role, Sosa will oversee the hotel’s culinary operations while driving menu development and leading the culinary team. He will also serve as a liaison between the hotel and Hilton’s culinary innovation team. Most recently, he served as complex executive chef for Hilton Portland Downtown and The Duniway, a Hilton Hotel, overseeing the culinary programs of both properties. “Daniel brings an impressive combination of culinary expertise, creativity and thoughtful leadership to Hilton McLean,” said Danielle Havey, general manager, Hilton McLean Tysons Corner. “His commitment to developing people and creating memorable guest experiences makes him an ideal leader for the next chapter of our culinary program. We are thrilled to welcome him to the team.” Sosa brings more than 13 years of experience with Hilton, with roles spanning Colombia, Panama and the United States. Throughout his career, he has led diverse culinary teams across restaurants, banquets and large-scale hotel food and beverage programs. Originally from Bogotá, Colombia, Sosa began his professional journey as an industrial designer before following his passion for food to Le Cordon Bleu in Ottawa, where he studied culinary arts. His training in both design and cuisine continues to shape his approach, balancing creativity, technique, presentation and the overall guest experience. “Joining Hilton McLean Tysons Corner is an exciting opportunity, and I’m honored to be part of a hotel with such a strong culinary and hospitality foundation,” said Sosa. “I’m excited to learn from the team, develop our chefs and build on the hotel’s culinary legacy. Great hospitality begins with great people, and I look forward to creating something together that our team, guests and community can be proud of.” Sosa describes his culinary philosophy as recognizable, approachable food that is thoughtfully executed and grounded in flavor. His design background also influences how he considers the function, presentation and evolution of each culinary experience. Colombian cuisine remains especially meaningful to Sosa because of its connection to home and family. Some of his earliest food memories are walking through local markets with his grandmother, snacking on raw green beans along the way. For him, its appeal extends beyond individual dishes and ingredients to the tradition of gathering around the table to talk, laugh and share stories. “I believe technique and presentation are important, but flavor always comes first,” Sosa added. “A great culinary program is never built around one chef. It comes from developing a strong team, respecting the ingredients, listening to our guests and delivering consistency while still leaving room for creativity.” As director of culinary, Sosa looks forward to refreshing the property’s menus, creating distinctive dining experiences and developing the hotel’s culinary talent. He also plans to foster strong partnerships across the property and within the surrounding community. That commitment to service has been a meaningful part of his career, including preparing meals with his Hilton team for families staying at Ronald McDonald House Charities of Oregon while their children received medical care. Outside the kitchen, Sosa enjoys spending time with his wife, traveling, exploring new cities and cultures and discovering restaurants along the way. The customizable format includes ingredients such as beans made daily, house-made sofrito and kebabs seasoned and cooked in-house. PINCHO is also moving to a rotating seasonal menu designed to introduce additional Latin-inspired flavors and ingredients throughout the year. The first seasonal item is the Harvest Bowl, or Cosecha Bowl, available through November. It features white rice, Latin-style roasted sweet potatoes, flame-roasted corn, rajas made with grilled poblano peppers and onions, Bravas and aioli sauces, chopped cilantro and the customer’s choice of protein. The roasted sweet potatoes, rajas and Bravas sauce have also been added to the Build Your Own Bowl customization lineup. PINCHO is supporting its catering business with an online ordering platform and a tiered rewards program. Customers automatically earn points toward Amazon gift cards on qualifying catering orders, with no enrollment required. The program includes three earning levels: Level 1: Three points per dollar on spending up to $5,000 Level 2: Four points per dollar on spending up to $10,000 Level 3: Five points per dollar on spending of $10,001 or more Every 100 points is equal to $1 in rewards. For example, a $1,000 qualifying order at the five-point level would earn $50 in Amazon gift cards. A customer’s tier resets 12 months after the first catering rewards order. Rewards apply only to catering-menu purchases, and qualifying spending excludes taxes, tips, fees, discounts and other non-menu charges. Customers receive an email from CateringRewards after checkout with information about viewing and redeeming their points. articles.title: Firebirds Raises Over $5 Million for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation
articles.titleKo: Firebirds Raises Over $5 Million for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Firebirds Wood Fired Grill (“Firebirds”), the award-winning, polished-casual American restaurant and steakhouse, today announced it has surpassed $5 million raised for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (“ALSF”), the largest independent childhood cancer charity in the U.S. The milestone marks a significant chapter in the brand’s ongoing partnership with the nonprofit, which was originally founded by Alexandra “Alex” Scott, whose childhood lemonade stand inspired a national movement to fund lifesaving pediatric cancer research and support families affected by childhood cancer. The proceeds raised by Firebirds have funded critical research projects, helped families travel for treatment, provided essential family assistance programs, and delivered crucial resources for children courageously battling cancer. “At Firebirds, we believe restaurants have the power to bring people together not only around the table, but around causes that truly matter,” said Steve Kislow, Chief Executive Officer of Firebirds Wood Fired Grill. “Reaching $5 million for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation is an incredible milestone, and we’re only getting started. We are honored to support an organization that has made such a profound impact in the fight against childhood cancer, and we remain deeply committed to helping advance its mission for years to come.” Since 2012, Firebirds has rallied behind year-round fundraising initiatives benefiting ALSF, effectively funding 100,000 hours of research. This 14-year partnership, supported by team members and guests across 23 states, reflects Firebirds’ broader commitment to community impact and purpose-driven hospitality. On an ongoing basis, Firebirds donates $1.25 from the sale of every Firebirds Lemonade to ALSF and deepens its commitment through its annual “Lemonade Days” event every June. For three days, team members set up lemonade stands at every Firebirds restaurant to raise funds, and for several weeks proceeds from lemon-based menu items – like a slice of 5 Layer Lemon Cake or a Tito’s Lemonade Drop martini – go to ALSF. Additionally, Firebirds hosts the ALSF Golf Classic each September and is a longtime sponsor of the annual Lemon Ball, a “yellow-tie” gala held in Philadelphia. Its team also regularly hosts children impacted by cancer across its system, offering an opportunity for their families to connect and enjoy a meal together. “Every dollar raised helps move us closer to better treatments and a cure for pediatric cancer, and $5 million truly moves the needle,” said Liz Scott, Co-Executive Director of Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation and Alex’s mom. “Firebirds has been an incredible partner to ALSF, and I’m thrilled to see them achieve this great milestone. Their impact has become even more valuable as they grow, and we are so grateful for the continued generosity and dedication of the Firebirds team and their guests. This support has made a real and lasting difference for children and families across the country.” Since its founding, Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation has become a nationally recognized force in pediatric cancer fundraising, helping raise hundreds of millions of dollars toward research into better treatments and cures while also providing emotional, financial and logistical support to families navigating childhood cancer diagnoses. Urbane Cafe, the California-born restaurant famous for fresh-baked focaccia, gourmet sandwiches and hand-crafted bowls, is bringing its signature scratch-made dining experience to Glendale, California. Opening Monday, September 28 at 249 Glendale Avenue, the new restaurant marks Urbane Cafe’s first location in the city and continues the brand’s expansion across Southern California. Founded in Ventura in 2003, Urbane Cafe was built on the belief that fast-casual dining shouldn’t require a compromise on quality. The brand has cultivated a loyal following with fresh focaccia baked in-house daily, gourmet sandwiches served with farm-fresh side salads, nourishing bowls, house-made sauces and more, all crafted with premium ingredients at an approachable price point. Creating a warm, relaxed alternative to the traditional fast-casual experience, Urbane puts its scratch kitchen and signature hearth oven at the center of the guest experience, allowing diners to see the care and craftsmanship that goes into making every dish. “Glendale is an exciting new chapter as we grow throughout Southern California,” said Tom Holt, Founder of Urbane Cafe. “We’ve always been intentional about where we open, seeking communities where we can put down roots, connect with our guests and become a part of the neighborhood. We’re excited to open our doors to Glendale and look forward to serving the community for years to come.” To celebrate its arrival, Urbane Cafe is inviting the Glendale community to join in a series of special grand opening promotions: ● Golden Tickets (September 18-24): Be on the lookout for physical tickets being handed out in the community, redeemable for a complimentary item during Grand Opening week. ● Order Online, Get Your Next Meal Free (September 28-October 4): Glendale guests who order online in the Urbane Cafe app during Grand Opening Week earn a free meal for their next visit. ● Teacher and Healthcare Worker Give Back Days (September 30 + October 7): Healthcare workers and teachers will have the opportunity to register for a promo code redeemable for a free sandwich, salad or bowl (online or in the app). They can reserve their meal via the Urbane Cafe Glendale Giveback Facebook event Pages. The Glendale opening marks another milestone in Urbane Cafe’s continued growth across Southern California and the Southwestern United States. The brand plans to open two additional Southern California locations by end of 2026, with an ambitious goal of reaching 100 locations in 2030 – adding more Las Vegas and Arizona communities to their mix. As Urbane Cafe expands, the company remains committed to a thoughtful growth strategy to maintain the integrity of its food and culture that has been central to the brand since its founding. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smokey Mo’s BBQ, the neighborhood barbecue franchise known for serving Texas classics smoked in-house daily with fast, friendly service, has named Von Dawson as its Vice President of Franchise Development as the company continues building its footprint across Texas. In his new role, Dawson will lead franchise development for Smokey Mo’s, with a focus on building the brand’s pipeline of qualified franchise partners and expanding its presence in new and existing markets across the state. His appointment comes as Smokey Mo’s continues strengthening the operational foundation behind its franchise growth, with an emphasis on restaurant-level performance, franchisee support and a model built to compete in today’s operating environment. Dawson joins Smokey Mo’s from Dine Brands Global, where he most recently served as Director of Franchise Sales, overseeing franchise sales across the company’s IHOP, Applebee’s and Fuzzy’s Taco Shop brands. Throughout his career in franchise development, he has worked with established restaurant brands to identify qualified operators, build franchise relationships and support development across new markets. Dawson is also a Certified Franchise Executive through the International Franchise Association. “Smokey Mo’s stood out to me because of how much opportunity there is ahead of the concept with its standout identity and operating model,” said Dawson. “Barbecue remains a relatively underserved category in franchising, which creates a unique opportunity for Smokey Mo’s to bring an established brand to more Texas operators and communities. There’s a strong story to tell prospective owners about the business, the team supporting them and the role they can play in what comes next. I’m looking forward to building on that foundation and introducing Smokey Mo’s to operators who see the same potential in this brand that I do.” Dawson’s appointment comes at a time when the brand has continued growing while staying focused on the fundamentals of the business. With 22 restaurants across the Austin, San Antonio and Houston areas and additional locations in development, Smokey Mo’s has taken a measured approach to expansion, strengthening restaurant operations and franchisee support while continuing to deliver the food, service and neighborhood experience that have kept guests coming back for more than 25 years. The brand’s franchise model combines a smaller restaurant footprint and lean labor structure with multiple dayparts and a growing catering business. Smokey Mo’s has also continued investing in restaurant design, kitchen efficiency and digital tools, including a redesigned website, PAR Online Ordering and PAR POS, to strengthen operations and the guest experience. “We’re thrilled to have Von join our leadership team and bring his depth of franchise development experience to Smokey Mo’s,” said Craig Haley, CEO of Smokey Mo’s BBQ. “He understands what experienced operators are looking for, how to build trust throughout the development process and what it takes to move from initial interest to opening restaurants. His perspective and track record will be instrumental as we look ahead to our next phase of growth in Texas.” As Smokey Mo’s BBQ franchise grows, the company remains focused on partnering with experienced operators who understand their local communities and see an opportunity to build scalable portfolios with the brand. Dawson will play a central role in identifying those partners and advancing the company’s development strategy across the state. Mokas Coffee & Eatery, known for its expertly roasted coffee, freshly baked pastries, and made-to-order breakfast and lunch offerings, is celebrating the grand opening of its newest location at 11814 S Fellows St, Olathe, KS, on Wednesday, September 30. The opening marks a major milestone for the brand as it’s the first location to open under franchisee ownership. As the first-ever Mokas franchisee, Christian Coleman plans to open a total of six locations across Johnson, Douglas, and Shawnee counties. The Olathe opening builds on another significant milestone for Mokas, which celebrated its 20th anniversary in November 2025. Grand Opening Celebrations Mokas will host a Friends & Family Day on Sunday, September 27 before the official opening, followed by a full grand opening celebration on Wednesday, September 30, complete with a ribbon cutting alongside the local Chamber of Commerce. The first wave of guests will be entered to win a $100 social media giveaway, and guests visiting the new café can spin a prize wheel for branded merchandise, tote bags, and gift cards, while supplies last. Throughout the first month of operation, Mokas will also partner with KidsTLC , donating 10% of all 16 oz specialty drink sales to the local nonprofit. “I’ve always been driven to create experiences that bring people together,” said Coleman. “Opening our first Mokas in Olathe is the realization of everything my team and I have been working toward. This community has already shown us so much warmth, and we can’t wait to bring that same Midwest hospitality to our guests every single day.” About the Local Owner Coleman brings a diverse hospitality and entrepreneurial background to his new venture. He launched his career in professional tennis at the BNP Paribas Open in Indian Wells, California, where he oversaw VIP operations, sponsorships, and hospitality, and later became the youngest professional Tournament Director in tennis. He is also the Founder & President of Midwest Restaurant Group, and also co-founded Sunnyland Kansas Farm, an 80-acre organic farm, and developed a 20,000-square-foot industrial hemp drying facility in Newton, Kansas. The new 3,100-square-foot café is expected to create between 45 and 60 new jobs in the Olathe community, with members of Coleman’s family also involved in supporting the business. Coleman has already signed on to build five additional Mokas locations across the Kansas City metro area, with the Olathe café serving as the flagship for that growth. “Christian embodies the entrepreneurial, hospitality-driven mindset we look for in franchisees,” said Jason Ingermanson, President of Mokas Coffee & Eatery and CEO of JRI Hospitality. “Watching him open the doors on our first-ever franchise location, after celebrating our 20th anniversary, is a full-circle moment for our brand. Christian sets the standard for how we’ll continue to grow across the Midwest.” Established in 2005, Mokas Coffee & Eatery offers a variety of everyday favorites including in-house roasted coffee, smoothies, energy drinks, and pastries, along with breakfast and lunch wraps, sandwiches, soups, and salads. With five corporate-owned locations operating in Salina, Colby, and three in Wichita, KS, three more under development in Wichita and Hays, KS, and its first franchise location now open in Olathe, Mokas is actively seeking passionate entrepreneurs to join the brand. articles.title: White Castle Opens in Daytona Beach
articles.titleKo: White Castle Opens in Daytona Beach
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . White Castle, America’s first fast-food hamburger chain and home of The Original Slider, opened its Daytona Beach Castle today with a celebratory ribbon cutting, fanfare and first-day Craver excitement. The opening marks the brand’s fourth freestanding Central Florida Castle and the newest chapter in a Florida expansion that has been building since 2021. Located at 1944 LPGA Boulevard just west of the I-95 interchange, the 3,430-square-foot Daytona Beach Castle features indoor and outdoor seating, two drive-through lanes and an iconic tower design with a sleek, modern-industrial flair. In place of traditional drive-through windows, hospitality doors let team members step outside and hand orders directly to guests in their cars, a hallmark of the modern Castle. On opening day, White Castle welcomed hundreds of excited fans — known as Cravers — with Sliders and smiles, and the first 105 guests through the doors received White Castle swag, a nod to the company’s 105 years in business. Opening day drew enthusiastic Cravers from across Central Florida and beyond, eager to be among the first to experience the highly anticipated location. VIPs attending the ribbon cutting included White Castle President Anthony Joseph, who was joined by family members and company leaders, local elected officials, community partners and invited guests. A White Castle grand opening is marked by lighthearted festivities, and the Daytona opening was no exception. The royal celebration began with a ceremonial processional, as the Daytona Beach team marched in bearing the Castle’s Scepter to the tune of the Entrance March from Act III of Johann Strauss II’s The Gypsy Baron . Next came The Passing of the Golden Scissors Ceremony, followed by the official ribbon cutting, a burst of confetti cannons and the long-awaited proclamation: “It’s a Castle!” “There is no better feeling than handing over the very first Sliders in a new community,” said Joseph. “A Castle truly becomes a Castle when neighbors walk through the doors, and Daytona Beach showed up for us today. We are grateful for such a warm welcome and look forward to being part of this community for generations to come.” Chief Marketing Officer Jamie T. Richardson added, “Every Castle takes on the personality of the place it calls home, and you could feel Daytona Beach’s spirit the moment the doors opened. From our hospitality doors to the Crave Case built for beach days, this Castle was designed to meet Cravers right where they are. Today’s turnout is a reminder of why we choose each new location so thoughtfully.” The Daytona Beach Castle brings more than 60 new jobs to Volusia County, continuing White Castle’s commitment to investing in the communities where it does business and cultivating talent from within. The restaurant is led by General Manager Kenneth Espinal, a dedicated member of the White Castle family since 2021. Community leaders welcomed the investment and the boost it brings to the LPGA Boulevard corridor. “It’s exciting for me to see another nationally recognized brand choose to grow in our community. White Castle’s investment reflects confidence in Daytona Beach, home to more than 91,000 residents. White Castle will offer another dining option to an already diverse restaurant scene,” said City of Daytona Beach Mayor Derrick L. Henry. (As a dedicated high school teacher in addition to his Mayoral duties, Mayor Henry was unable to attend; he was represented by Volusia County Commissioner Dannette Henry during the festivities). The Daytona Beach Castle joins the Orlando flagship, the largest White Castle in the world and the site of the brand’s celebrated 2021 return to the Sunshine State; the Clermont Castle, which opened in 2025; and the Kissimmee Castle, which opened in May 2026.
