articles.originalSummary: The team behind South African-inspired restaurant Kudu are returning to their South East London heartland with the opening of a wood-fired rotisserie chicken concept. Called Braai Bird, the restaurant will open on the former Kudu Grill site on Nunhead Lane this November and will serve a menu centred on wood-fired rotisserie chicken, slow-cooked over wood and served with South African sauces, including its signature monkey gland sauce, and sharing sides. Chef and co-founder Patrick Williams will oversee the food, while creative director and co-founder Amy Corbin has worked with Lithuanian designer Liga Piraga on the restaurant’s interiors. The restaurant’s interiors will retain elements of the former site and include bespoke artwork by South African artists. An open kitchen at the rear of the restaurant will feature the wood-fired rotisserie as a central element of the operation. Braai Bird marks a return to Peckham for the couple, who opened Kudu on Queens Road in 2017. The pair subsequently opened Curious Kudu, a gallery and private dining space, and Kudu Grill, which focused on South African braai cooking using wood and charcoal in the area.

articles.title: Can Burger King Sustain Momentum? It Starts with What’s Still Left to Do
articles.titleKo: Can Burger King Sustain Momentum? It Starts with What’s Still Left to Do
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A year ago, Sami Siddiqui fielded a similar question. What’s something people ask about Burger King, Popeyes, Tim Hortons, and Firehouse Subs owner Restaurant Brands International that surprises him? Or, similarly, what’s a topic he wonders doesn’t surface more often? Siddiqui, RBI’s CFO, and former president of Popeyes, speaking at the Barclays 19 th Annual Global Consumer Conference, said his response hasn’t changed much, year-over-year. But it has shifted a bit. The company, as you’d guess, gets a lot of asks about Burger King’s U.S. business, which represents about 17 percent of RBI’s operating income. Those still dominate the conversation. Yet people have begun progressing from questioning when a turnround will come to if it’s sustainable. Burger King U.S. in Q2 posted same-store sales growth of 8.5 percent (10 percent two-year stack). That outpaced the larger QSR burger field by north of 9 percentage points. And it followed a Q1 result of 5.8 percent (4.7 percent two-year). The narrative for Burger King throughout Reclaim the Flame, which turned four years old on September 9 , is none of it was flash-in-the-pan devised. articles.title: Why Snacking is the New Growth Opportunity for QSRs
articles.titleKo: Why Snacking is the New Growth Opportunity for QSRs
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The trend is especially strong among younger consumers. The afternoon slump. The post-gym protein run. The after-school treat. The late-night craving. For today’s consumers, these moments are becoming just as important as breakfast, lunch and dinner—and they’re creating a growing opportunity for limited-service restaurants. Snacking is no longer an occasional indulgence. It’s become an eating occasion of its own. Yet while consumers are reaching for snacks throughout the day, many aren’t looking to restaurants to satisfy those cravings. Mintel reports that 80 percent of consumers snack more than once a week, but only 36 percent purchase snacks from foodservice more than once a week. Several trends are fueling the shift to snacking. Some consumers’ busy schedules compel them to replace traditional meals with smaller options, while health-conscious diners are looking for protein, energy and functional ingredients to power them through the day. At the same time, social media has fueled a “little treat” mindset, where consumers reward themselves with an affordable indulgence such as a sweet bite, specialty beverage or savory snack that brightens an ordinary day. The trend is especially strong among younger consumers. According to Datassential, more than 40 percent of Gen Z consumers say they’re snacking more than they were a year ago. They’re also highly influenced by social media, making limited-time offerings and visually appealing menu items powerful traffic drivers. The good news? Operators don’t have to reinvent their kitchens to capitalize on the snacking trend. Many of the ingredients needed to create craveable snacks are already sitting in the walk-in cooler or pantry. The key is looking at them differently. That basket of fries can become loaded fry flights with rotating toppings. Cinnamon roll dough can transform into bite-sized cinnamon sugar poppers served with cream cheese icing or caramel dipping sauce. Tortillas can become dessert crisps dusted with cinnamon sugar and paired with fruit dip or chocolate sauce. Chicken can be reimagined as snack wraps, handheld skewers or buffalo chicken dip. Extra pizza dough can become garlic knots, dessert bites or stuffed snack pockets. Breakfast ingredients offer even more flexibility. Consider mini pancakes with flavored butter, French toast bites with dipping sauces, or breakfast sliders served all day to satisfy consumers looking for a quick afternoon pick-me-up. Existing bakery items like donuts and cookies can find a second life as bread pudding bites, ice cream sandwiches or inclusions in blended desserts. Beverages present another major opportunity. Rich’s consumer research found that more than half of consumers sometimes replace a snack with a beverage, particularly when it’s portable, convenient or offers perceived health benefits. Protein shakes continue to gain popularity, yet indulgence still wins attention. Dessert-inspired milkshakes, fruit smoothies topped with cold foam, dirty sodas, seasonal refreshers and globally inspired flavor combinations can all create excitement while delivering strong margins. Perhaps most importantly, snacks create new occasions to visit. Consumers may not stop for a full meal at 3 p.m., but they’ll swing through the drive-thru for a shareable order of loaded tots, a handheld dessert or a limited-time shake they discovered on TikTok. The winning snack menus won’t necessarily feature dozens of new products. Instead, they’ll showcase familiar ingredients presented in fresh, unexpected ways that encourage impulse purchases, social sharing and repeat visits. articles.title: Yardbird Southern Table & Bar Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: Yardbird Southern Table & Bar Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Yardbird plans to continue operating during the bankruptcy process as it pursues a going-concern sale. Florida-based Yardbird Southern Table & Bar filed for bankruptcy on Sunday with plans to sell its business after expansion costs, restaurant-level operating challenges, pandemic disruptions, and mounting debt strained its finances. The polished-casual concept currently operates company-owned restaurants in Dallas, Washington, D.C., and Chicago, along with licensed locations in Las Vegas and Singapore. The company employs approximately 508 people across its corporate and licensed restaurants. Yardbird plans to continue operating during the bankruptcy process as it pursues a going-concern sale. The company filed several first-day motions seeking permission to maintain payroll and employee benefits, pay certain vendors, continue customer programs, and use existing cash systems. The filing lists approximately $24.8 million in funded debt and an estimated $24.2 million in unsecured claims. Brightwood Loan Services and related lenders are owed roughly $13.3 million under a credit agreement backed by first-priority liens on nearly all of Yardbird’s assets. City National Bank of Florida is owed nearly $8.4 million through a Main Street Lending Program loan, and approximately $3.1 million is outstanding under an agreement with restaurant financing and rewards platform inKind. Yardbird was founded in Miami Beach in 2011 and became known for fried chicken, Southern-inspired dishes, weekend brunch, bourbon dinners, and an extensive cocktail and wine program. The business opened a licensed Las Vegas restaurant in 2015. A private equity sponsor invested in the company in 2017 as Yardbird moved into a period of expansion. The chain subsequently opened restaurants in Los Angeles, Dallas, Washington, D.C., Chicago, Denver, and Singapore. The sponsor became the sole owner of Yardbird Group in 2025 after separating from the company’s founders. The expansion required substantial spending on leases, restaurant construction, architecture, and design. Yardbird took on additional debt to finance those openings and related capital expenditures. The COVID pandemic complicated the growth effort by closing dining rooms, reducing sales, accelerating reliance on delivery, and changing traffic patterns in several urban markets. Performance eventually diverged across Yardbird’s portfolio. Some restaurants continued to perform well, but others struggled with changes in tourism, convention business, consumer behavior, neighborhood traffic, and nearby development. Losses from underperforming restaurants increased pressure on Yardbird’s liquidity. The company closed its Denver restaurant in 2025, followed by its Los Angeles and Miami locations in 2026. It also implemented turnaround plans and made changes to its senior team in an effort to direct resources toward stronger restaurants. Debt maturities continued to create problems despite the closures and cost-saving efforts. Yardbird attempted to restructure its loan with City National Bank, which matured in August 2025, but the parties did not reach an agreement. City National Bank sued several Yardbird entities in March for breach of contract and enforcement of the loan documents. The lender has filed a motion for summary judgment, and Yardbird faces an October 1 deadline to respond. The company began exploring a sale as its liquidity position tightened. Soravine Advisors launched a marketing process in August and contacted more than 170 prospective buyers, including restaurant groups and financial investors. Twenty-one parties signed nondisclosure agreements. Yardbird ultimately received three nonbinding indications of interest for all or part of the company, but each offer came in significantly below the value of its first-lien debt. articles.title: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.titleKo: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.originalSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date. Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience. Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed. Central patios, generous proportions, fountains, handcrafted materials and lush greenery give the space its structure and soul, evoking the kind of environment that takes decades to settle into its surroundings. Antique furniture sits alongside bespoke pieces, and reclaimed terracotta, natural stone, marble and aged timber are used throughout, materials that carry history and wear it well. “People rarely talk about specific design features. They talk about the atmosphere,” adds Alexis. “If people leave believing the space possesses a history, then we have succeeded in creating something that feels authentic rather than constructed.” A considered selection of suppliers and craftspeople underpins the interior. Sogni and Pooky provide the lighting, Pierre Frey and Morris the fabrics and upholstery, and Mandarin Stone the marble and stone surfaces. Flexhouse – responsible for custom joinery, millwork and bespoke fabrication – also contributed to the furniture alongside vintage pieces and Leta, while Resources delivered the decorative wall finishes. Together they bring a layered quality to the space, as though each element has its own provenance and story. With its new 280-cover restaurant, hacienda-inspired interiors and striking luminescent bar stocked with more than 2700 bottles, Tigermilk Spitalfields invites guests into what feels like the brand’s thirteenth home. Through a considered interior scheme full of texture and attention to detail, the restaurant offers a transportive South American-inspired experience designed to engage every sense.

articles.title: Elysium Retreats Unveils Major UK Expansion Strategy with up to 12 New Retreat Destinations Under Consideration
articles.titleKo: Elysium Retreats Unveils Major UK Expansion Strategy with up to 12 New Retreat Destinations Under Consideration
articles.originalSummary: UK retreat operator, Elysium Retreats , has unveiled plans for a major UK expansion programme, targeting up to 12 new destinations over the next two years as demand for high-quality nature-led escapes continues to grow. Part of the Sight Acre Group, Elysium Retreats brings together distinctive countryside and waterside stays designed around nature, comfort and memorable time away. The brand is already established through two UK destinations: Fairwood Lakes in Wiltshire, home to waterside lodges, woodland lodges and a unique floating lodge, and Benview Lodges in Stirlingshire, where guests can enjoy peaceful lodge stays surrounded by rolling Scottish hills, close to Aberfoyle and on the edge of Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park. With demand for premium UK staycations remaining strong and travellers increasingly seeking nature-focused experiences, Elysium Retreats is accelerating plans to build a nationwide collection of distinctive retreat destinations. The expansion will be delivered through a combination of acquisitions, the refurbishment of existing holiday and leisure parks, and the development of new retreat destinations in carefully selected locations across the UK. The growth programme forms part of the brand’s wider ambition to become one of the UK’s leading retreat operators, creating a collection of locations that each have their own character and sense of place, while sharing the same focus on comfort, nature, warm hospitality and meaningful guest experiences. articles.title: Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase 2027
articles.titleKo: Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase 2027
articles.originalSummary: Hospitality businesses from across the UK are being invited to bring along their outstanding apprentices to the annual Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase (HAS), taking place at the House of Commons during National Apprenticeship Week. The event, to be held on Wednesday 10 February 2027, from 12.30pm–3.30pm in the Terrace Pavilion, House of Commons, will bring together around 120 hospitality apprentices from many of the UK’s leading operators for an afternoon celebrating the talent, ambition and professionalism of the industry’s future leaders. Over the past decade, more than 1,800 hospitality apprentices have attended the Showcase, making it one of the sector’s most prestigious events dedicated to recognising apprentice achievement. The Showcase provides apprentices with a rare opportunity to meet their local MPs, demonstrate their skills, share their personal career journeys and hear from leading figures from both the hospitality industry and Government. It also gives Parliamentarians the opportunity to see first-hand the contribution apprentices make to one of the UK’s most important sectors and the vital role hospitality plays in supporting employment, skills and economic growth. Hospitality is one of the UK’s largest employers, offering careers across hotels, restaurants, pubs, contract catering, visitor attractions and events. Apprenticeships continue to provide an essential pathway in the industry, helping employers develop skilled, motivated teams while creating rewarding long-term careers for thousands of people every year. The HAS event celebrates not only the achievements of individual apprentices but also the commitment employers make to developing future talent. Every apprentice attending has a story to tell, whether they have progressed from entry-level roles into management, discovered a passion for professional cookery, or built confidence and skills through workplace learning. The event has become one of the highlights of National Apprenticeship Week, shining a spotlight on the diverse and rewarding careers hospitality offers and challenging outdated perceptions of the industry. Hospitality businesses of every size, from independent operators to national brands, are encouraged to bring along their apprentices who have demonstrated commitment, enthusiasm and a passion for the industry. Whether they are just beginning their careers or have already achieved significant milestones, the Showcase offers a unique opportunity to recognise their success on a national stage.

articles.title: Brook & Green Opens on Chiswick High Road, Bringing an 89-Cover All-Day Neighbourhood Concept and Wine Room to W4
articles.titleKo: Brook & Green Opens on Chiswick High Road, Bringing an 89-Cover All-Day Neighbourhood Concept and Wine Room to W4
articles.originalSummary: Brook & Green , a new all-day restaurant and wine room, will open at 142 Chiswick High Road at the end of September 2026 , bringing an ingredient-led dining concept and a dedicated wine room to one of West London’s most established neighbourhood dining streets. The opening lands at a pivotal moment for the site. Chiswick High Road has long been one of the capital’s most reliable neighbourhood catchments – affluent, residential, and driven by repeat local use rather than destination trade – and Brook & Green has been conceived to serve that demand directly, built for regular, all-day use rather than a single occasion. The concept occupies 89 covers across three distinct spaces: 49 at ground floor, 14 on the terrace, and 26 in a newly developed wine room downstairs, built around the restaurant’s own working wine collection. The all-day format has been designed to evolve through the day, from breakfast and lunch through to evening dining and drinks, with the wine room offering a separate, slower-paced destination for pre-dinner drinks, wine discovery and private dining. The kitchen’s output is food-first and ingredient-led, drawing on Mediterranean, Asian and British influences across an all-day menu built for consistency and repeat use rather than occasion-only dining. Breakfast runs from 8am until 11:30am on weekdays and 12:30pm at weekends. The all-day à la carte menu takes over from midday, running until 11pm Monday to Thursday and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays; Sundays are restricted to brunch and lunch, closing at 6pm. The wine room opens from 5pm. Interiors have been reworked around a warmer, more craft-led identity: a softened bar as the room’s social anchor, new booth seating, linen drapery and layered lighting, and a communal table dressed with large-scale artwork. Downstairs, the wine room’s exposed brickwork, integrated bottle display and warm joinery shelving give it a distinct character from the room above. The refit has been led by B3 Designers , the hospitality-focused design studio whose mission is to help ambitious operators turn bold ideas into enduring hospitality brands through strategy and story-driven design. The wider turnaround and redevelopment has been directed by Savvy IQ , the hospitality consultancy that led the project from initial market and feasibility study through to concept finalisation. Tim Price, Owner-Operator of Brook & Green, said: “This isn’t about building a name around one person or one kitchen – it’s about building a restaurant Chiswick will use every week, for years. That’s a different discipline to running a destination restaurant, and it’s exactly what we set out to do here.” Brook & Green’s launch adds to a run of openings and reinvestment along Chiswick High Road, reflecting a broader shift among neighbourhood restaurants towards all-day, multi-daypart formats that maximise use of a single site rather than committing to one service period. The opening will create 18-19 new roles.

articles.title: How Bars Can Build Stronger Teams and Reduce Turnover
articles.titleKo: How Bars Can Build Stronger Teams and Reduce Turnover
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bar work is demanding. Employees deal with late nights, physically intensive shifts, customer pressure, and unpredictable schedules. The best bars are not built on great cocktails alone. They are built on teams that work efficiently, communicate clearly, and stay committed through busy seasons and changing customer demands. Yet one of the biggest challenges in hospitality is constant staff turnover. Replacing bartenders, barbacks, and service staff repeatedly drains time, money, and energy, making it difficult for any venue to maintain consistent service. Creating a high-performing bar team requires more than hiring talented people. It involves building an environment where employees feel supported, challenged, and motivated to stay. The good news is that reducing turnover is often less about offering extravagant perks and more about improving everyday management practices. Why Turnover Happens So Often in Bars Bar work is demanding. Employees deal with late nights, physically intensive shifts, customer pressure, and unpredictable schedules. When these challenges are combined with poor communication or limited opportunities for growth, even skilled bartenders begin looking elsewhere. Common causes of turnover include: Inconsistent management expectations Limited training after onboarding Unclear career progression Burnout from scheduling practices Lack of recognition for strong performance Understanding these factors allows owners and managers to focus on retention rather than constant recruitment. Hire for Team Fit, Not Just Technical Skill A technically strong bartender who struggles with collaboration can create more problems than someone with slightly less experience but excellent communication skills. During hiring, evaluate how candidates respond to feedback, work under pressure, and contribute to team dynamics. Behavioral interview questions can reveal qualities such as adaptability, accountability, and customer-service mindset. These traits are often more difficult to teach than drink preparation techniques. Create a Structured Onboarding Process Many bars lose employees within the first few weeks because new hires never feel fully integrated. A structured onboarding process helps employees understand expectations and become productive faster. Effective onboarding should include: Clear service standards POS system training Bar setup and closing procedures Customer interaction guidelines Shadow shifts with experienced staff Scheduled feedback check-ins When new employees know exactly what success looks like, they are more likely to gain confidence and remain engaged. Invest in Continuous Development Training should not stop after the first week. Ongoing learning keeps employees motivated and improves service consistency across the entire team. Short weekly skill sessions, cocktail workshops, upselling practice, and guest-service scenarios can significantly improve performance over time. Many successful operators implement regular bar team trainings that focus on both technical execution and teamwork. These sessions reinforce standards while giving staff opportunities to ask questions and contribute ideas. Build Clear Career Pathways One of the strongest retention tools is showing employees that staying with the business leads to growth. Even in small operations, career progression can be clearly defined. Examples include: Barback to bartender Bartender to lead bartender Lead bartender to bar manager Bar manager to beverage director When employees understand how they can advance, they are more likely to invest in the success of the business. Schedule to Prevent Burnout High performers often receive the busiest shifts, but consistently overloading top employees can lead to exhaustion and eventual resignation. Fair scheduling practices are essential. Managers should monitor: Consecutive late-night shift

Heat levels range from country, with no heat, to angry, the brand’s most intense level, with several options in between. Made-to-order chicken is paired with sides including mac and cheese, coleslaw and fries, giving Sacramento guests plenty of ways to build a meal around their preferred combination. “Sacramento has a great food culture, and we’re excited to finally bring Angry Chickz to the city,” said David Mkhitaryan, CEO and founder of Angry Chickz. “This opening is an important step for the brand as we continue growing throughout California and introducing more people to what makes Angry Chickz different. articles.title: Just Salad Launches New Creative Campaign with NBA Star Jalen Brunson
articles.titleKo: Just Salad Launches New Creative Campaign with NBA Star Jalen Brunson
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Just Salad, the fast-casual restaurant chain committed to making everyday health and sustainability possible, launched its first creative campaign with Jalen Brunson, point guard for the New York Knicks and 2026 NBA Champion and Finals MVP. Built on the creative platform “New York Always Knew,” the campaign puts two New York fandoms side by side — the guests who knew Just Salad was onto something back when it was a single storefront, and the fans who knew Brunson was something special well before everyone else caught on. “We were doubted a lot, and for a long time. We didn’t get much attention and some people thought we weren’t cool enough,” said Nick Kenner, Founder and CEO of Just Salad. “But we kept our heads down and focused on making the product and the experience better every single day. That grit and focus on substance and winning is what aligns us with Jalen; his fans never needed convincing either. This campaign is about those shared values.” Just Salad opened its first restaurant in 2006 with a reusable bowl program already in place, years before that kind of sustainability commitment was common in restaurants, and has grown to more than 125 locations largely on the strength of guests who say they knew the brand was different long before the concept of fast casual salad became a category. That same instinct — spotting the real thing early — is the throughline the campaign asks Brunson’s fans to recognize in him. The centerpiece is a documentary-style CTV spot that pairs Brunson’s own story with real fan testimonials, shot to feel like New York telling its own story rather than a traditional endorsement. “What I like about this campaign is that it feels true to how this partnership came together. I was already a fan of Just Salad, and being able to build something with a New York brand I genuinely believe in makes this really meaningful to me,” said Jalen Brunson, 2026 NBA Champion, NBA Finals MVP and Captain of the New York Knicks . “New York fans can tell when something is authentic, and I think this captures that.” That fandom plays out differently by market. Across New York City and Long Island, outdoor creative carries the line “Real New Yorkers Know” — a nod to the fans who were paying attention early. In New Jersey and Connecticut, the same spirit shows up as “We Always Knew,” extending that sense of ownership to the fans across the wider tri-state footprint who claim both Brunson and Just Salad just as fiercely. “Just Salad fans have believed in this brand since long before we had 125 locations to point to,” said Jen Lally, Chief Marketing Officer of Just Salad . “Jalen’s fans have that same instinct — the pride of recognizing greatness before everyone else caught on. New York is the heart of this campaign, but that feeling of seeing something special early, and knowing you were part of it from the start, is universal.” As the long-term partnership develops, Brunson is expected to engage with Just Salad’s leadership and culinary teams, visit restaurants, connect with guests and bring his perspective into the business over time. articles.title: Surcheros Brings Back Guest Favorites, Including Mini Quesadilla
articles.titleKo: Surcheros Brings Back Guest Favorites, Including Mini Quesadilla
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Surcheros is bringing back three guest favorites. Beginning September 21, the Mini Burrito and Mini Quesadilla return to the menu at all Surcheros locations, joined by banana peppers on the Fresh Toppings bar. The Minis have a devoted following, and those guests made sure Surcheros knew it. Requests came in through the app, at the counter and across social media, and the brand listened. On Sept. 21, the Mini Burrito and Mini Quesadilla are back where they belong. “Our guests told us what they missed, and we listened,” said Luke Christian, founder and CEO of Surcheros. “The Minis have always had a loyal following. Bringing them back is our way of saying thank you to the people who kept asking for them by name.” The Mini Burrito starts with a 10-inch flour or wheat tortilla and comes with chips and salsa. Guests choose grilled chicken, ground beef, or carnitas, with grilled steak available for an extra cost, then load it up from the full Fresh Toppings bar and finish it with a sauce. It is the same build guests know from the Surcheros Burrito, sized for a lighter appetite. The Mini Quesadilla is built on an 8-inch flour tortilla and served with chips and salsa. It starts with cheese, takes the guest’s choice of meat and toppings, and is grilled and folded before serving. The Mini items are back on the menu for guests who want everything Surcheros does well in a smaller portion. They have long been a go-to for a lighter lunch, and for anyone who wants to leave room for queso or guacamole on the side. Banana peppers rejoin the Fresh Toppings bar the same day, available on any build-your-own entrée for guests who like a little tang without much heat. articles.title: HB Protein Smoothies Inks 6-Unit Deal with Franchising Investor Bob Morris
articles.titleKo: HB Protein Smoothies Inks 6-Unit Deal with Franchising Investor Bob Morris
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HB Protein Smoothies, a protein-first smoothie concept built for today’s health-conscious consumer, signed a six-unit development agreement with Bob Morris, a franchise investor with a multi-unit track record in Planet Fitness and 7 Brew Coffee. Morris will open five locations in Broward County and one in Martin County, marking the brand’s fourth multi-unit signing in Florida since March. Morris has spent more than two decades building and operating franchise businesses, including ownership stakes in Planet Fitness dating back to 2004 and 7 Brew Coffee drive-through locations he has developed in New York State over the past three years. He said he runs every new concept through the same checklist before signing on, and HB Protein Smoothies cleared it. “I like the simplicity of the operation, the limited scope of offerings, and the low labor factor,” Morris said. “It also has strong second-generation real estate potential, so you don’t need to start in Class A space. It checks off a lot of boxes.” Morris’ track record is part of what makes the deal notable. He knows what it takes to scale a simple, high-frequency concept across multiple units, and he is applying the same playbook to HB Protein Smoothies. “Honestly I’ve had some winners and losers, and you keep plugging away and know what to look for the next time,” Morris said. “This one checks the boxes I look for.” Morris said his first visit to the Scottsdale store, where he saw professional athletes stopping in as regulars, confirmed his decision. “It was phenomenal. No aftertaste, spot-on flavoring, and filling,” he said. “I’ve had plenty of protein shakes that never lived up to the hype. This one did.” Morris plans to run his Florida units alongside his son and daughter, with an experienced operator on staff to guide the buildout. “It’s something we can all do and grow together,” he said. “Bob has already built and scaled multi-unit operations in two other categories, so when he tells us the model works, that carries weight,” said Daniel Boone, co-founder of HB Protein Smoothies. “Having an operator with his track record commit to six units in South Florida is proof the concept holds up outside Scottsdale.” “When someone with Bob’s résumé, Planet Fitness, 7 Brew, and decades of real estate development, commits to six units, it tells us everything they need to know about where this brand is headed,” said Dan Rowe, CEO of Fransmart, HB Protein Smoothies’ franchise development partner. US Foods 2026 Fall Scoop From bar and grill to casual dining concepts, Italian-inspired dishes remain a mainstream global flavor platform across American menus. With 55% of consumers often choosing global flavors when dining out1, Fall Scoop offerings include premium pasta, versatile dough, upgraded shareables, chef-driven proteins and flavorful finishing touches that can help operators create differentiated Italian-inspired dishes across dayparts without adding unnecessary back-of-house complexity. From a risotto sourced from Italy that comes together in minutes to a Neapolitan-style pizza dough that performs beautifully across various applications, our new lineup helps operators bring quality and consistency to their menus to help boost profitability and increase customer satisfaction.” Restaurant operators continue to navigate high food and labor costs while looking for ways to keep menus fresh, deliver value and create memorable dining experiences. Fall Scoop meets those needs with products that pair culinary appeal with practical benefits, from ready-to-use sauces and fully cooked proteins to frozen items that help reduce prep time, support portion consistency and minimize waste. Fully cooked and individually frozen in 4-ounce portions, this item helps operators serve consistent sweet Italian sausage in minutes for pizzas, pastas, sandwiches and center-of-plate dishes. articles.titleKo: Tropical Smoothie Cafe Adds New Salted Caramel Javablender Smoothie
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Tropical Smoothie Cafe is upgrading morning routines with the new limited-time Salted Caramel Javablender Smoothie. Now available at participating cafes nationwide, the smoothie blends the bold flavor of cold brew coffee with the creamy, craveable experience guests expect from Tropical Smoothie Cafe. Cold coffee continues to gain momentum in the U.S., with Americans spending roughly $17.7 billion on out-of-home cold coffee in 2023, more than double the $8.5 billion spent in 2016, according to Technomic data. The Salted Caramel Javablender Smoothie puts a spin on that daily ritual, combining cold brew coffee with caramel sauce, Chobani Sweet Cream Zero Sugar and nonfat yogurt, topped with salted caramel crunch for added texture. With 180 mg of caffeine, it delivers roughly the same amount of caffeine as two 8-ounce cups of brewed drip coffee. Coffee isn’t the only way Tropical Smoothie Cafe fuels the morning. Pairing caffeine with protein can help support sustained energy throughout the day. The Salted Caramel Javablender Smoothie is available as part of the Smoothie & Breakfast Pair & Save offering, with protein-rich favorites from the all-day breakfast menu, including: PB Protein Crunch Bowl with 32g of protein Sausage, Egg & Cheese ‘Dilla with 27g of protein Mixed Berry Greek Yogurt Bowl with 26g of protein All American Wrap with Sausage with 17g of protein “Morning routines are personal, and for many people, coffee is the spark that gets things moving,” said Deborah von Kutzleben, Chief Marketing Officer, Tropical Smoothie Cafe. “With the Salted Caramel Javablender Smoothie, we’re giving guests a new way to enjoy that ritual — one that feels a little more fun, a little more craveable and unmistakably Tropical Smoothie Cafe. It’s an easy pairing with breakfast for anyone looking to add something different to their day.” Whether guests are looking to switch up their usual coffee run or order their morning caffeine with a protein-packed breakfast favorite, Tropical Smoothie Cafe is giving them a new way to start the day. Breakfast menu availability and prices may vary by location. For more information or to find a cafe near you, visit www.TropicalSmoothie.com. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Round Table Pizza, FAT Brands’ pizza franchise known for its signature flavors and premium ingredients, is giving fans another reason to gather around the table this football season. In collaboration with Dr Pepper and The Dairy Alliance, the pizza chain is introducing the first Dr Pepper-inspired pizza nationwide, alongside an all-star lineup of limited-time menu items inspired by the bold, one-of-a-kind flavor of the beloved beverage. Available now through Jan. 3, the new menu features a winning combination of pizza, wings and shareable sides built for Dr Pepper fanatics and flavor seekers alike. Leading the lineup is the Dr Pepper BBQ Pizza, featuring Round Table Pizza’s signature crust layered with creamy garlic sauce and Dr Pepper BBQ sauce, a sweet-and-smoky creation that blends Dr Pepper’s signature flavor with Round Table’s BBQ sauce. The craveable pizza is then topped with a three-cheese blend, crispy bacon, mini pepperoni, and finished with an extra drizzle of Dr Pepper BBQ sauce and fresh green onions. Fans can also dig into the Dr Pepper BBQ Classic or Boneless Wings, coated in Dr Pepper BBQ sauce and topped with crispy bacon for the ultimate flavor kick, and the Bacon & Cheese Tots with Dr Pepper BBQ Dipping Sauce, delivering the perfect side for snacking. Also joining the seasonal menu is Round Table Pizza’s Margherita Pizza, a timeless favorite topped with marinara sauce, a melty three-cheese blend, fresh whole milk mozzarella, Italian herb seasoning and fresh whole-leaf basil. “Dr Pepper has an incredibly passionate fan base and an unmistakable flavor, which gave us an opportunity to create something people haven’t experienced before,” said Corry Reid, VP of Marketing for Round Table Pizza. “The result is a bold lineup that brings together great pizza, big flavor and shareable favorites made for feeding the whole crew.” “Dr Pepper fans are always up for bold flavor, and a Dr Pepper-inspired pizza definitely delivers,” said Trish Riddle, SVP Foodservice at Keurig Dr Pepper. “By bringing our signature 23 flavors to Round Table Pizza’s game day lineup, we’re giving fans a new way to enjoy the one-of-a-kind taste they already love—this time by the slice.” The post Round Table Introducing Dr. Pepper-Inspired Pizza Nationwide appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Tijuana Flats Revives its Viral Two-Pound Burrito
articles.titleKo: Tijuana Flats Revives its Viral Two-Pound Burrito
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Some burritos are built for lunch. The Mega-Freakin’-Juana is built for the challenge. Tijuana Flats is bringing back its viral, two-pound Mega-Freakin’-Juana Burrito for a limited time, giving Flatheads another chance to go big, go hungry and see just how much burrito they can handle. Flatheads get first dibs of the Mega-Freakin’-Juana, with early access starting on Monday, Sept. 21. The fully loaded, seriously oversized burrito is ready to give guests a whole lot more to love. Guests can build their burrito with their choice of protein and beans, cilantro lime or Mexican rice, lettuce, tomatoes, onions, sour cream, jalapeños and cheddar jack cheese. Then, because one tortilla isn’t enough, the whole thing is wrapped in two flour tortillas and toasted until golden brown. Fully loaded, tightly wrapped and served with a side of “how am I supposed to finish this?” Every Mega-Freakin’-Juana Burrito comes with a side of chips, because Tijuana Flats believes you should never underestimate the appetite of someone taking on a 2-pound burrito. “We’ve never been afraid to go a little overboard, but even we had to ask ourselves if a 2-pound burrito was a little freakin’ ridiculous,” said Ashlley Lemke, Director of Marketing at Tijuana Flats. “Some people told us two pounds was insane. We said ‘hold my queso’ and built it anyway. It’s huge, it’s loaded with fresh ingredients, and it absolutely works.” The Mega-Freakin’-Juana Burrito is available for dine-in, carryout, online ordering and third-party delivery where available. Pricing starts at $15.99 for veggie and climbs to $21.99 for steak. Guests can pick their protein, customize their fillings and bring an appetite big enough for the occasion. The Mega-Freakin’-Juana joins a menu built around fresh-to-order Tex-Mex favorites that guests can make their own from burritos and tacos to quesadillas, chimichangas, bowls and salads. At Tijuana Flats, guests can get their food “Tijuana Style” or however they wanna, with plenty of ways to customize their meal. Ready to go full Megajuana? Visit one of Tijuana Flats’ 100 locations across Florida, Alabama, North Carolina and Kentucky. At Tijuana Flats, loyalty comes with perks. Members of Flathead Rewards earn one point for every dollar spent, plus access to exclusive rewards, deals, bonus-point opportunities and instant rewards just for signing up. Guests can download the Flathead Rewards app at https://qrco.de/bbUMoR. For more information and to find a location near you, visit www.tijuanaflats.com. articles.title: Cheesecake Factory and Flower Child Continue to Compete with ‘Everybody and Nobody’
articles.titleKo: Cheesecake Factory and Flower Child Continue to Compete with ‘Everybody and Nobody’
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Cheesecake Factory EVP and CFO Matthew Clark is no stranger to questions about Flower Child. “Many, many” have poured in from the investor community, he said, asking about a brand that joined the polished casual giant’s portfolio seven years ago when it purchased North Italia and Fox Restaurant Concepts (where Flower Child resided) for about $308 million. Cheesecake Factory originally bought in three years earlier, in 2016, when it grabbed a minority stake under a deal that allowed it to later acquire full ownership. North Italia touted nine stores. Flower Child—just two years old at the time—had five. Today, there are 50 of the Italian casual concept and 40 of the fast casual (there are 220 or so Cheesecake Factory locations). As is often the case on Wall Street, Clark said, investors understand but probably underappreciate the emerging chain’s path. Flower Child will expand at a pace that makes sense for the brand, he explained, whether it concerns site selection, labor, or just making sure it has the right management unit-by-unit. “And so, I think, we’re continuously reeducating,” Clark said during the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “Wall Street just loves growth. And we want to make sure that it’s quality growth.” It is understandable, however, why investors would wonder if Cheesecake Factory is going to press on the pedal. Flower Child posted same-store sales gains of 13 percent last quarter (17 percent two-year stack). Roughly 8 points flowed from traffic, with 2.5 percent pricing and an added check lift from catering. That spiked annualized average-unit volumes to $5.4 million alongside adjusted mature store-level margins of 20.1 percent. A few older restaurants posted $6.5 million to $7 million. For perspective, if Flower Child was one of the top 50 grossing QSRs in the country ( per the QSR 50 ) by systemwide sales, its AUV would slot fourth, ahead of McDonald’s ($4.088 million) and behind In-N-Out ($6.032 million). Shake Shack follows at $4.048 million. Flower Child’s AUV would also rank second on QSR’s Contenders list , trailing Portillo’s ($8.5 million) and fronting Jollibee ($4.990). The $5.4 million sailed fellow publicly traded fast casual sweetgreen ($2.677 million). Flower Child is a vibe, and one that appeals to families, adults, and everything in between. Still, Flower Child is hardly in idle state. Clark said the company aims to step into the 20–25 percent growth range. For the full fiscal year, seven are expected to open, as well as five to six Cheesecake Factory boxes, six to seven North Italias, and as many as seven of FRC’s other concepts, like The Henry (a recent opening, in Chicago suburb Wilmette, pushed $10 million Year 1 AUVs at weekly sales of $200,000). Clark said Flower Child boasts the best unit economics of Cheesecake Factory’s suite. It’s about 33 percent cash-on-cash returns. It also has the largest total addressable market given it fits any geography, smaller or larger cities, and more. Additionally, the company knows when it densifies, as it’s done in Dallas and Phoenix, performance increases alongside awareness. It’s a brand uplifting from growth rather than being concerned about sales transfer. And why has Flower Child carved such a defined counter-service niche? Clark said the company internally calls it, “The Cheesecake Factory fast casual.” It’s not assembly line. The setup is scratch kitchen, open concept, where customers see food being made as they come in. “And it’s got a huge, defensible moat,” Clark said, “because not only does it have the price point of fast casual, the breadth of the menu, it’s got a vibe in the restaurant.” If you unpack four quadrants of business potential, he added, Flower Child splits through opportunities. articles.title: Krispy Kreme Releases New Churro Doughnut Dots
articles.titleKo: Krispy Kreme Releases New Churro Doughnut Dots
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Krispy Kreme is giving fans a new reason to make their fall doughnut run even sweeter with the debut of all-new Churro Doughnut Dots – a poppable, shareable treat made with Krispy Kreme’s signature light and airy dough, tossed in cinnamon sugar and paired with a delicious dulce de leche dipping sauce. Available for a limited time beginning Tuesday, Sept. 22 at participating shops nationwide, each order of Churro Doughnut Dots includes eight cinnamon sugar-coated Doughnut Dots served with a rich dulce de leche dipping sauce for dipping and dunking. “Churro Doughnut Dots are such a fun way to bring a little extra sweetness to fall,” said Alison Holder, Chief Product and Brand Officer at Krispy Kreme. “They start with our proprietary light and airy dough, then we toss them in cinnamon sugar and pair them with a delicious dulce de leche dipping sauce. They’re poppable, dippable and the perfect add-on to your Krispy Kreme purchase.” Whether guests are grabbing an Original Glazed® dozen, picking up fall favorites, making a coffee run or bringing treats to share, Churro Doughnut Dots are an easy way to add a little cinnamon-sugar joy to the order. Dip them, dunk them, share them – or keep them close. We get it. Krispy Kreme’s Churro Doughnut Dots will be available in-shop, via drive-thru and for pickup or delivery through Krispy Kreme’s app and website, while supplies last. The Churro Doughnut Dots join Krispy Kreme’s ongoing Autumn Seasonal Collection , featuring two all-new doughnuts, two returning fan-favorites and two beverages that offer the comforts of autumn in every sip. Visit www.krispykreme.com/locate/location-search to find a shop near you and share how you’re enjoying Churro Doughnut Dots by using #KrispyKreme and tagging @krispykreme on social media. To learn more about this limited-time offering, visit www.krispykreme.com/promos/churro-donuts. The post Krispy Kreme Releases New Churro Doughnut Dots appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Carl’s Jr. Challenges Burger Rivals with Free Angus Maximus Offer
articles.titleKo: Carl’s Jr. Challenges Burger Rivals with Free Angus Maximus Offer
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Carl’s Jr. is calling on burger fans to hand over their crowns and experience the difference of a freshly cooked-to-order burger through its “Stealing the Crown” promotion. For a limited time, My Rewards loyalty members can submit a picture of a crown, or their receipt from a royally disappointing burger from the competition, via direct message on Instagram to Carl’s Jr., signifying their surrender to a better burger from Carl’s Jr. In return, guests will be rewarded with a promo code for a complimentary Angus Maximus, the hero LTO of their Burger Revolution, in the My Rewards app. “Carl’s Jr. believes the next burger battle will be won on quality,” said Burge Diemer, chief marketing officer at Carl’s Jr. “A burger worth fighting for shouldn’t be waiting for you in a holding cabinet — it should hit the grill when you order it. With ‘Stealing the Crown,’ we’re inviting burger fans to surrender the crown and taste the difference for themselves with an Angus Maximus cooked fresh specifically for them.” The promotion builds on Carl’s Jr.’s new cooked-to-order initiative, designed to deliver hotter, fresher and more consistently craveable burgers. Rather than relying on traditional holding systems that can compromise temperature and flavor, Carl’s Jr. begins cooking burgers after a guest places an order and are served hot and fresh from the charbroiler. The Angus Maximus Available at $5.99 for a limited time at participating locations, the Angus Maximus is the first limited-time offer item to launch under the brand’s “Burger Revolution.” At 5.7 ounces, the Angus Maximus delivers 100% Angus beef at $1.05 per ounce, making it a standout value and quality among major fast-food burger offerings. It features two charbroiled, 100% Angus beef patties seasoned with Carl’s Jr.’s signature blend, melted American cheese, sliced onions, dill pickles and special sauce, all served on a buttery toasted brioche bun. For more news, follow Carl’s Jr. on social media. For promotions, download the Carl’s Jr. app and join the My Rewards loyalty program. articles.title: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opens First Massachusetts Location
articles.titleKo: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opens First Massachusetts Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bubbakoo’s Burritos, the award-winning Mexican-fusion concept, announces the grand opening of its first Massachusetts location in Brockton. The new restaurant is located at 735 Belmont Street in a high-visibility commercial retail plaza and is owned and operated by Payal and Deep Patel. The brand’s debut in the state marks another step in its continued East Coast expansion, building on its established presence throughout the region. “Brockton has been our home for 20 years, so we know this community well and wanted to bring something different to the city,” said Payal Patel. “Bubbakoo’s stood out to us because there really is something for everyone, and guests have the freedom to create a meal that’s their own. We’re looking forward to introducing the brand to our neighbors and welcoming the community through our doors.” To celebrate the grand opening, the first 50 guests to make a qualifying purchase will receive a year’s supply of free burritos, with one free burrito per month for a year. Guests can explore Bubbakoo’s signature Mexican-fusion menu, featuring customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas and more. Additionally, the new location opens in time for guests to take advantage of Bubbakoo’s fall menu and seasonal promotions. Guests can try the brand’s newest menu additions, including Fried Cauliflower, available as both a starter and protein option, and Apple Pie Egg Rolls. Throughout the rest of September, Bubbakoo’s Rewards members can also participate in the Season Ticket loyalty promotion, earning 15 bonus BubbaKoin on qualifying visits and a free entrée reward after their fourth visit. Additional promotions throughout the month include Triple Score Sundays, food holiday offers and 15% off catering for fall gatherings. “Opening our first restaurant in Massachusetts is an important step as we continue to grow Bubbakoo’s presence in New England,” said Chris Ives, CEO of Bubbakoo’s Burritos. “The Northeast is a familiar region for our brand, and we see a lot of opportunity to build on our roots and introduce Bubbakoo’s to more communities throughout the area. With Payal and Deep’s strong connection to Brockton, we’re confident they’ll be great partners as we establish our presence in Massachusetts.” Over the past 17 years, Bubbakoo’s Burritos has become a fan favorite for its unique menu, superb customer service, and welcoming dining environment. Living up to its promise to “create something different,” the brand offers more than 12 signature flavors that fuel its ever-evolving lineup, from the Papi Hibachi steak and shrimp Burrito, to the Crispy Buffalo Chicken Quesadilla, Nashville Hot Crispy Chicken Burrito, California Steakhouse Burrito, and more. Guests are encouraged to blend creativity with the fresh, high-quality ingredients Bubbakoo’s has to offer. Bubbakoo’s Burritos has established a prominent U.S. presence across the country, creating a dedicated legion of fans. Since its inception in 2008, Bubbakoo’s has grown from its Jersey Shore roots to more than 140 locations across 17 states. The brand has been recognized among Franchise Times’ Top 40 Smartest-Growing Franchises, Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500, QSR Magazine’s Top 50 Contenders, and the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in America. articles.title: Five Pieces of Advice to New Restaurant CEOs to Survive Their First 100 Days
articles.titleKo: Five Pieces of Advice to New Restaurant CEOs to Survive Their First 100 Days
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The measure of the first 100 days will be whether the employees who show up to serve them every day feel like the restaurant and their jobs are finally being steadied. I’ve spent four decades watching new chief executives walk into their first day in one of two ways—certain they understand the job or, just as they’re closing their office door for the first time, saying out loud, “What do I do now?” The reality is that the person certain of what they’re going to be doing will find out quickly that the job they acquired and the job they imagined were two different things. Their first 100 days running the company will determine far more than first quarter numbers. This happens often in the restaurant and fast-service industry, especially those trying to rebound from a crisis. New Cracker Barrel CEO Dave Deno is currently experiencing this pressure, with more emotional weight than most incoming executives ever face. Cracker Barrel is more than just a restaurant chain to its customers. It’s a piece of personal history for millions. That’s precisely why the connections made internally and externally in his first 100 days will determine far more than first quarter numbers. Having worked with restaurant executives in dire situations, I know the chair they’re sitting in rather well, and I know why they were selected. So let me provide what I’d offer any new restaurant chain or group CEO walking into a wounded, watched, and wary organization. 1. Time is shorter than you think, and shorter than it should be. The average tenure of a CEO in the United States runs a little over three years. Deno is inheriting a company that just lived through an activist fight and a rebrand that had to be reversed within days of launch. The board and the shareholders looking to restore their restaurant’s reputation are going to be impatient. Use the early days deliberately. Focus on avoiding the two typical mistakes new leaders tend to make. The first is to recognize that new CEOs are going to bring change, and change causes fear throughout an organization until the new leader is trusted. The second urgent and ongoing concern is to communicate, communicate, communicate. Your goal in the early going is to build trust. Getting out into the restaurants to meet people at every level will tend to build trust and reduce the fear that comes when new top management takes over. 2. Resist the urge to prove yourself with another big swing. The single clearest lesson from what happened at Cracker Barrel is that fast, sweeping change introduced without the guest and employee base walking alongside you is premature boldness. It’s just exposure. I’ve watched this pattern destroy CEOs who mistook activity for progress. It’s critical for these new CEOs to demonstrate that they actually listen before they act, and then to act with appropriate speed. 3. Share your version of the story or it will be silenced by someone else’s version. This is the mistake I see destroying more executives than any strategic miscalculation ever does. When a company goes quiet during a period of uncertainty, the vacuum gets filled by activist investors, media narrative, and employee speculation. If new CEOs are inheriting a restaurant chain or group that just lived through exactly that dynamic, they must start communicating directly and frequently from day one: short, honest updates to their own people first, in their own words, before they ever need a quarterly earnings call to explain themselves. 4. Get out of headquarters and into the restaurants. A restaurant’s culture lives outside of their main corporate office. It lives on the floor, with the servers and cooks who show up every day regardless of what’s happening in the boardroom. articles.title: Subway Leans into Value with ‘Feed Your SUBconscious’ Campaign
articles.titleKo: Subway Leans into Value with ‘Feed Your SUBconscious’ Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The campaign will appear across broadcast and streaming television, streaming audio, digital, social media, in-restaurant and other owned channels. America: when it comes to today’s overpriced, unsatisfying and inconvenient food choices, stop settling. You know and deserve better. And beginning right now, Subway is here to help more than ever – by getting inside your head. Today, Subway enters a new era with the launch of “ Feed Your SUBconscious ,” a brand platform starring actor and comedian Will Arnett that reinforces Subway as the go-to better-for-you choice at a great value. Everyone has a SUBconscious, the inner voice that knows there is a simpler, better way to eat. When considering greasy fast food, pricey bowls and other food that doesn’t satisfy, your SUBconscious is right there, encouraging you to enjoy freshly sliced meats, loads of veggies and bread baked daily – the kind of delicious, satisfying food Subway has served for more than 60 years. Subway’s bold and hilarious Feed Your SUBconscious platform gives that inner voice a face – actually, several faces – all played by Arnett. In the initial anthem launching today, Arnett transforms into five distinct characters, each representing the voice that appears when a craving strikes or a food decision needs to be made. From smoothie counters to burger drive-thrus, each character delivers the sharp, funny and occasionally irreverent guidance people need to stop settling and make the better choice. Subway and Arnett will continue to introduce America to the characters as Feed Your SUBconscious evolves. The campaign will appear across broadcast and streaming television, streaming audio, digital, social media, in-restaurant and other owned channels. “Most advertising tries to convince people of something. This campaign begins with something they already know,” said Jeff Klein, Chief Marketing Officer, Subway. “They know when they’re settling for a meal they do not really want and when lunch is about to become an afternoon regret. Feed Your SUBconscious gives that instinct a voice, with Will Arnett reminding people that Subway offers satisfying, freshly prepared food, made exactly how they want it, with value that makes the choice even easier.” Arnett brings the exact tone and range the SUBconscious needs. Across five distinct characters, he makes that inner voice hilarious, believable and memorable, while delivering the tough love we all sometimes need. “If you know what’s good for you, you’ll listen to me, because I AM you!” Arnett said. “We don’t need to settle for a nap on a sesame seed bun or pay ridiculous prices for pond water. Let’s remember how much we crave delicious, affordable food that keeps us going … and go to Subway.” With thousands of U.S. restaurants, a robust third-party delivery network and expanded hours at many locations, a better meal choice at Subway is a convenient choice for almost any American who listens to their SUBconscious. Every Subway sandwich is made to order and built exactly the way each guest wants it. Veggie-forward, lean-protein and good source of fiber choices are available across the menu at a compelling value. So, America, beginning today, join Subway in this new era by listening to your SUBconscious. You’ll be proud and satisfied that you did. articles.title: Gong cha’s New Growth Model Lands at UCSF and UC Berkeley
articles.titleKo: Gong cha’s New Growth Model Lands at UCSF and UC Berkeley
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Gong cha, the world’s leading bubble tea brand with nearly 2,200 locations across 33 international markets, is expanding its nontraditional presence through a new Proud to Serve partnership with Ladle & Leaf at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) and UC Berkeley. The locations are now serving Gong cha’s freshly brewed, customizable beverages alongside Ladle & Leaf’s menu of scratch-made soups, salads and sandwiches. The partnership gives students, faculty, healthcare professionals and campus visitors convenient access to Gong cha while demonstrating how the brand can enter high-traffic university and healthcare environments beyond the traditional storefront. Expanding Gong cha’s Proud to Serve Model Gong cha’s Proud to Serve program allows established foodservice operators to add the brand’s freshly brewed teas within their existing venues, creating new points of distribution while maintaining the product quality and consistency associated with Gong cha. The licensing model enables operators to activate an additional revenue stream with a globally recognized beverage brand using minimal equipment and a format that integrates seamlessly into their existing footprint and operations. “The Proud to Serve program is an important part of how we are building Gong cha’s presence beyond the traditional storefront,” said Michael Nedelkovich Jr., Vice President of U.S. Non-Traditional Franchise Development at Gong cha. “UCSF and UC Berkeley are the types of high-traffic, community-driven environments where Gong cha can become part of consumers’ daily routines. Our partnership with Ladle & Leaf demonstrates the flexibility of this model and creates a blueprint for expanding into more campuses, hospitals and other nontraditional destinations nationwide.” Guests at Ladle & Leaf’s UCSF and UC Berkeley locations can choose from a variety of Gong cha offerings, including premium milk teas, fruit teas, freshly brewed teas, matcha beverages and the brand’s signature milk foam teas. Each beverage is handcrafted and can be customized by sweetness, ice level and toppings. Gong cha is known for sourcing premium teas from leading tea estates in Asia, brewing its teas fresh throughout the day and preparing its tapioca pearls daily. The brand’s emphasis on quality and freshness complements Ladle & Leaf’s existing focus on wholesome meals made with premium ingredients. “Our goal has always been to provide delicious, wholesome food made with care,” said Steve Sarver, Chief Executive Officer of Ladle & Leaf. “Adding Gong Cha allows us to pair our fresh soups, salads, and sandwiches with one of the world’s leading premium bubble tea brands. We believe it’s the perfect refreshing complement to our menu.” Creating a Blueprint for Nontraditional Growth The openings reflect Gong cha’s broader strategy to reach consumers across more of the places where they study, work, travel and gather. Through Proud to Serve partnerships with established foodservice operators, Gong cha can expand into new venues while offering operators an established global brand with a flexible, complementary beverage platform. The model also enables Gong cha to build awareness among new consumers and establish a repeatable pathway into similar university, healthcare and institutional environments. Alongside its expanding presence on campuses, Gong cha is pursuing additional opportunities across hospitals, airports, restaurants and other high-traffic destinations. Supporting Gong cha’s Broader U.S. Expansion Nontraditional development complements Gong cha’s continued franchise growth as the brand works toward surpassing 500 locations across the Americas by 2028. articles.title: Market Place Food Hall reveals traders for Victoria Station opening
articles.titleKo: Market Place Food Hall reveals traders for Victoria Station opening
articles.originalSummary: Market Place Food Hall has revealed the full list of traders for its upcoming site at London Victoria Station set to open on Friday 16 October. The trader line-up, featuring 10 operators, will include Argentinian Grill, serving flame-grilled meats and steaks; Hide & Greek, offering gyros, wraps and loaded fries; and Inamo Sukoshi, specialising in sushi and Japanese-inspired street food. Other operators include Jollof Mama, serving West African dishes inspired by Nigerian flavours; Caribbean-Indian concept Limin; Italian pizza specialist Made in Puglia; Korean-inspired SABA; Latin American trader Streat Latin; Thai House; and The Duck Shed, which will serve duck wraps, burgers and other duck dishes. The food hall, first announced this summer and described by the brand as the UK’s first station-based food hall, will be located in Victoria Place Shopping Centre, with entrances from the station concourse, taxi rank and Eccleston Bridge. Spanning 5,000sq ft, it will seat 180 guests and feature a central bar serving cocktails and craft beer, and screens showing live sport and train departure information.

articles.title: SusieCakes to Open in Dallas’ West Village Neighborhood
articles.titleKo: SusieCakes to Open in Dallas’ West Village Neighborhood
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . SusieCakes, the beloved all-American bakery known for its nostalgic, scratch-made desserts, will officially open its newest Dallas location in West Village on Saturday, October 3. Located at 3699 McKinney Ave., Suite 318, Dallas, TX 75204, the new bakery marks the brand’s latest expansion in North Texas and brings SusieCakes’ signature cakes, cupcakes, cookies and other classic treats to the heart of Uptown Dallas. The West Village bakery will be located within the iconic pedestrian-oriented shopping center and will offer SusieCakes’ full menu of made-from-scratch desserts for birthdays, celebrations and everyday occasions. Twenty years ago, founder Susie Sarich opened the first SusieCakes with her grandmothers’ handwritten recipe cards, a commitment to baking everything from scratch using simple ingredients, and the belief that the best desserts are timeless classics that bring people together. Since then, SusieCakes has continued to grow, with the West Village bakery marking its seventh location in Texas and fourth in the DFW Metroplex, while remaining committed to the same recipes, values and baking philosophy that have defined the brand since day one. “Opening in West Village is a wonderful next step as we continue to grow SusieCakes in Dallas,” says Susie Sarich, Founder and CEO of SusieCakes. “As a Dallas resident, it’s been special to see firsthand how warmly the community has embraced SusieCakes. West Village is such a vibrant neighborhood, and we look forward to welcoming guests in and being part of even more celebrations, both big and small.” Since opening the first bakery in 2006, SusieCakes has become part of countless birthdays, graduations, weddings, baby showers and everyday celebrations. SusieCakes is best known for its signature Vanilla Celebration Cake, custom-decorated layer cakes and freshly baked cupcakes, each generously frosted with indulgent buttercream. The bakery’s menu also features a variety of classic layer cakes, including Southern Red Velvet, Old-Fashioned Chocolate and Marble, alongside rotating seasonal desserts inspired by the holidays. Guests can also enjoy a selection of nostalgic baked goods, including chocolate chip cookies, snickerdoodles, and flourless peanut butter cookies. To celebrate the West Village opening, SusieCakes will host a Grand Opening Celebration from 12–3 p.m. on Saturday, October 3, with special giveaways, music, samples and an opportunity to meet founder Susie Sarich in person. The bakery will be open from 10 a.m.–7 p.m. on opening day, with festivities including: Free SusieCakes mugs for the first 50 guests, beginning at 10 a.m. with purchase, limited to one per guest A raffle for the chance to win free cake for a year The opportunity to meet Susie Sarich in person DJ tunes and complimentary samples from 12–3 p.m. The October 3 opening marks the latest chapter in SusieCakes’ continued growth in Texas while bringing the bakery’s nostalgic, made-from-scratch approach to one of Dallas’ most vibrant shopping and dining destinations. Golden Corral, the nation’s go-to buffet for variety and value, is adding All-You-Can-Eat Wings to the buffet for a limited time, with plenty to look forward to on game days. Guests can enjoy returning Bone-In Buffalo Wings alongside NEW Boneless Buffalo Bites, with both available as part of the All-You-Can-Eat Wings lunch and dinner lineup, now available across all Golden Corral locations. “We’re taking our All-You-Can-Eat Wings up a notch this year with Boneless Buffalo Bites,” said Darryl Mickler, Senior Vice President of Food & Beverage at Golden Corral. “Paired with our returning Bone-In Buffalo Wings, they give wing fans two styles to choose from while keeping that classic Buffalo flavor at the center.” For guests planning to feed a crowd outside the restaurant, Golden Corral is introducing two $25 Wing To Go offers through Oct. 18. Guests can choose 25 Bone-In Buffalo Wings for $25 ($1 a wing) or 50 Boneless Buffalo Bites for $25 (50 cents per bite) through GoldenCorral.com or the Golden Corral App, excluding third-party delivery sites such as DoorDash, Grubhub, and Uber Eats. The offers are available just in time for football watch parties, tailgates, and fall gatherings. “Golden Corral is all about bringing high-quality variety and value to the table, and our All-You-Can-Eat Wings are a great example of that,” said Lance Trenary, CEO of Golden Corral. “With our returning Bone-In Buffalo Wings, NEW Boneless Buffalo Bites, and two $25 To Go options, there’s something for every wing fan, whether they’re enjoying the buffet with family or picking up wings for a gameday gathering. We’re excited to give guests even more ways to enjoy the variety and value they’ve come to expect from Golden Corral.” Rounding out the fall lineup are Green Apple Lemonade and Green Apple Citrus Splash, both introduced Sept. 14. Guests can also enjoy Golden Corral’s wings through To Go, Individual Meals, and Platter options, including Weigh & Pay, Delivery, and Online Ordering. Golden Corral Rewards Members can expect other America $2.50 Value Deals throughout the rest of the year. articles.title: Long John Silver’s Announces $1.99 Wings Deal
articles.titleKo: Long John Silver’s Announces $1.99 Wings Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Long John Silver’s is bringing a new contender to game day, and it’s golden, crispy, and only $1.99 for three. Beginning Sept. 21, new Crispy Battered Wings feature tender chicken freshly battered in restaurants using Long John Silver’s signature batter. Pair them with the Baja or Sweet Chili dipping sauce for an extra layer of flavor. Guests can enjoy them on their own or go bigger with the new Game Day Platter, featuring wings alongside shrimp, Fried Pickles, and other Long John Silver’s favorites. “Guests already love our Chicken Planks, and wings gave us a fun way to bring our signature batter to something new,” said Meredith Smith, director of brand marketing at Long John Silver’s. “That familiar Long John Silver’s crunch feels right at home on a wing, and we can’t wait for guests to try them on game day.” Three Wings for $1.99? articles.title: Chili’s Turnaround Clears Way for New Restaurant Growth
articles.titleKo: Chili’s Turnaround Clears Way for New Restaurant Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s has approved 15 restaurants for fiscal 2028 and another 15 for fiscal 2029. Chili’s is ready to grow its restaurant count again. After spending the past several years repairing its existing business, the casual-dining giant plans to reach 2–3 percent annual unit growth and open as many as 30 restaurants per year by fiscal 2029. The company has identified more than 300 trade areas where it believes the brand can add locations, providing what CFO Mika Ware described as visibility into a decade of development. Chili’s is considering several paths for expansion. The company will continue building in major suburbs, but it has also identified openings in smaller communities, existing markets that can support infill development, and areas on the edges of growing metropolitan regions. Conversions offer another route. Chili’s could repurpose individual restaurant properties or acquire a small regional chain for its real estate if the economics are favorable. Ware said that tactic could prove useful in densely developed markets such as the Northeast, where suitable sites are more difficult to find. The pipeline is already forming. Chili’s has approved 15 restaurants for fiscal 2028 and another 15 for fiscal 2029. An additional 46 deals are in progress. New restaurants are expected to cost between $5 million and $6 million. The company believes those investments can produce attractive returns based on Chili’s current average unit volumes of $5 million and restaurant-level operating margins exceeding 18 percent. Locations constructed during the past three to five years have opened strongly and continued to outperform the brand’s averages. Chili’s plans to maintain discipline as development accelerates. Ware said the company does not want pressure to meet a numerical target to lead it toward weaker sites. The pace must also allow the chain to recruit and prepare enough general managers and team members to support each opening. The company’s internal development programs are expected to supply much of that restaurant talent. RISE prepares newer managers interested in becoming general managers, and LEAD trains general managers who could advance to director of operations positions. Most new restaurant leaders are expected to come from inside the company, although Chili’s recent performance has also helped it attract outside candidates. The development opportunity spans the country. Chili’s sees room for additional restaurants in established states such as Texas, Florida, and California, as well as underdeveloped territories in the Pacific Northwest, Southeast, and Midwest. Texas and Florida continue to benefit from population growth and new real estate development. Eight restaurants are already in the pipeline across those states. Chili’s also sees whitespace in Washington, where it has a limited streetside presence compared with competing casual-dining brands. The company recently acquired 10 franchised locations in Alabama and has identified five additional sites in the state. Chili’s owns development rights across all 50 states, giving the company flexibility to build in territories that were historically controlled by franchisees. Restaurant reimaging will create another source of growth. Chili’s completed 11 remodels during fiscal 2026 and has 70 projects in progress for fiscal 2027. The company plans to renovate roughly 10 percent of its system annually beginning in fiscal 2028, equal to approximately 110 restaurants per year. The first 16 completed projects carried an average cost of $600,000 per location. That figure included $100,000 for bar renovations that will only be required at an estimated 20 percent of the chain’s restaurants. The other 80 percent should cost closer to $500,000 per project. “Right now, in those early restaurants, we are getting a 3 percent to 5 percent sales lift, and that is on top
