articles.title: Stonefire Grill Supporting Cystic Fibrosis Foundation
articles.titleKo: Stonefire Grill Supporting Cystic Fibrosis Foundation
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Stonefire Grill, a premier fast-casual family dining destination for more than 25 years, serving generous portions of scratch-made, classic American-inspired dishes, is proudly supporting the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation to further the Foundation’s efforts to improve the lives of people with cystic fibrosis and advance the search for a cure. From Sept. 9 to Oct. 6, guests at all Stonefire Grill and Rattler’s Bar B Que locations throughout Southern California can donate and pen handwritten messages of support on blue ribbons, which will be displayed at Stonefire Grill and Rattler’s Bar B Que restaurants to drive greater awareness for the cystic fibrosis community. Stonefire Grill and Rattler’s Bar B Que will match guest donations up to $5,000. “In my 26 years with the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation, I’ve seen firsthand what CF means for people and families close to me,” said David Youngberg, CEO of Stonefire Grill. “Bringing our restaurant communities together behind the Foundation’s groundbreaking work is something I care deeply about. The blue ribbons in our restaurants are simple but powerful reminders that every contribution makes a difference, and that our guests are standing with the cystic fibrosis community in its goal of making CF stand for Cure Found.” Guests at Stonefire Grill and Rattler’s Bar B Que locations can take part by donating at the register and adding their name and personal message to a blue ribbon, which will be displayed throughout the restaurants. Guests ordering online directly through the Stonefire Grill or Rattler’s Bar B Que websites can round up their order total and contribute to the campaign. Deeply rooted in the Southern California communities they serve, Stonefire Grill and Rattler’s Bar B Que are proud to deliver an opportunity for guests to come together and give back to a cause that makes a difference for people and families affected by CF. Guest donations will help advance the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation’s critical efforts to improve the lives of people with CF. “The Cystic Fibrosis Foundation is deeply grateful for the support of Stonefire Grill,” said Shaina Flesser, Executive Director, Southern California Chapter of the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation. “Their generosity, alongside the CF community’s efforts, will build on our work that has helped add decades of life for people with CF. We are focused on supporting people with CF no matter where they are on their journey and on pursuing a cure for all people with the disease.” The post Stonefire Grill Supporting Cystic Fibrosis Foundation appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Buffalo Wild Wings GO Opening in Glen Allen on September 22
articles.titleKo: Buffalo Wild Wings GO Opening in Glen Allen on September 22
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The wait for wings is getting a lot shorter in Glen Allen. Buffalo Wild Wings GO opens Tuesday, Sept. 22, at 11446 W. Broad St., giving Henrico County a spot built entirely around ordering ahead and grabbing a bite to eat on the go. Opening day comes with a delicious reason to show up early: the first 50 guests in line, ages 18 and older, will receive FREE wings for a year.* Belle Holdings, Inc., owns and operates the restaurant under Franchisee Kevin Donham. Glen Allen marks the group’s 10 th Buffalo Wild Wings location in Virginia, joining restaurants in Richmond, Fredericksburg, Charlottesville and Culpeper. “We’ve been keeping tabs on Glen Allen for a while, and the demand here made the decision easy,” said Kevin Donham, franchisee of Belle Holdings, Inc. “The convenience of this format is that it doesn’t slow you down. You order ahead, you pull up and you have dinner on the table before kickoff.” The GO format highlights the parts of the menu that travel best — bone-in and boneless wings, chicken dippers, sandwiches, wraps and shareable sides, with 26 signature sauces and dry rubs to work through. Digital ordering and quick pickup make it a fit for busy weeknights, group orders and game-day spreads without a table reservation or a wait. BurgerFi is giving guests a reason to celebrate National Cheeseburger Day on Friday, September 18 with a Buy One BurgerFi Double Cheeseburger, Get a Second for $1 deal. This all-day, in-store-only promotion is available at participating BurgerFi locations while supplies last. Guests can enjoy up to two redemptions per customer of this all natural, hormone and antibiotic-free angus beef burger with American cheese, lettuce, tomato, and Fi sauce. “National Cheeseburger Day is our favorite holiday at BurgerFi and we always look forward to celebrating with our guests,” stated Paola Remus, VP of Operations and Training at BurgerFi. “All of our locations are ready to welcome our returning guests and first-time diners to take advance of the buy one double cheeseburger and get the second for $1 deal.” Beyond the classic BurgerFi cheeseburger, BurgerFi’s chef-curated menu features a premium lineup of craveable favorites, including all-natural Angus beef burgers, hand-breaded chicken tenders, fresh-cut fries made in-house, and hand-crafted, beer-battered onion rings fried to crispy perfection. Guests can also indulge in hand-spun custard shakes in chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, and Oreo along with chef selected seasonal offerings. BurgerFi delivers flavor without compromise, focusing on clean, high-quality ingredients. Guests can enjoy these new fall favorites alongside popular menu staples like the indulgent Wagyu-blend CEO Burger, the crave-worthy Rodeo Burger, and all-natural 100% Angus beef classics. National Cheeseburger Day only comes around once each year, and BurgerFi is ready to celebrate with a rare deal. Guests are encouraged to stop by their local BurgerFi on September 18 to enjoy the offer while supplies last and make the most of the brand’s fan-favorite cheeseburger celebration. articles.title: Sightline OS Launches Intelligent Inventory Solution Continuity AI
articles.titleKo: Sightline OS Launches Intelligent Inventory Solution Continuity AI
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Sightline OS, the inventory and supply chain platform built for multi-unit restaurant chains, today announced the launch of Continuity AI, an intelligent engine that maintains optimum inventory levels throughout the supply chain. Supply chain teams have historically had to pull together forecast, inventory, and supplier data from multiple sources to manually triage and figure out where action is needed to prevent menu outages. Too often, restaurants find out about a supplier or distributor outage only when it’s already started impacting their restaurants and guests. The supply chain team then must drop everything they’re doing to chase substitutions, expedite, and rebuild orders – firefighting instead of running the business. Now, Continuity AI identifies supply gap risks up to 12 weeks in advance, quantifies the severity of the disruption, whether it’s still preventable, and recommends exactly what to do next. The diagnosis, investigation, and solution is automated with AI so the restaurant can jump straight to proactive, preventative action with the full picture in place. “Restaurant supply chain has always been a hands-on business. I learned that early on as an entrepreneur driving my own food distribution delivery trucks and later leading supply chain teams inside some of the industry’s most complex restaurant organizations,” said Yusha Hu, co-founder and CEO of Sightline OS. “Continuity AI is about giving teams the ability to be proactive and preventative by identifying what’s coming, understanding what actually requires attention, and taking action before a disruption reaches the restaurant. That means less time analyzing and firefighting, and more time making decisions, building relationships and improving the business.” Sightline’s work with Bonchon shows what that shift can look like in practice. Since implementing Sightline OS, Bonchon’s system-wide weighted average distributor fill rate rose 1.1% to reach 99.3%, while dramatically reducing product substitutions across a network of more than 150 restaurants and 35 distributor operating companies. “Sightline OS has transformed how we manage our supply chain. With greater visibility across our distribution network and stronger forecasting capabilities, our team can identify potential inventory challenges earlier, collaborate more effectively with our partners, and improve supply reliability for our franchisees. That translates to fewer disruptions and a better experience for both operators and guests,” said Suzie Tsai, CEO of Bonchon. The Problem: Stockouts Are a Manual, Reactive Guessing Game For supply chain teams at multi-unit restaurant chains, figuring out why a menu item is out of stock, and what to do about it, is still largely a manual process. There’s no consistent way to quantify risks, no simple way to tell which disruptions are still fixable versus already a lost cause, and by the time a team understands the root cause, they’re often already reacting to an outage in progress rather than preventing the next one. The cost compounds quickly: lost revenue when guests can’t order what they want, brand erosion from repeat disappointment, and supply chain teams stuck firefighting instead of planning ahead. What Continuity AI Does Continuity AI is a reasoning layer built into Sightline OS that activates automatically the moment an inventory escalation is flagged. For every issue, it delivers: Early Warning + Forward Scan — flags products already out of stock or trending toward it based on available supplier lead times, and scans ahead for additional stockouts hiding later in the planning horizon. Impact Score (0–100) — a single severity score, plus a Critical/High/Medium/Low label, so teams instantly know which open issue matters most. articles.title: Swig Kicks Off Seventh Annual Save The Cups Campaign
articles.titleKo: Swig Kicks Off Seventh Annual Save The Cups Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Swig, Home of the Original Dirty Soda, is kicking off its seventh annual Save The Cups campaign, created to support women navigating breast cancer treatment while also promoting early detection. This year, Swig aims to raise at least $650,000 to help even more women and families facing breast cancer, building on the impact the campaign has made since its launch in 2020. THE STORIES THAT DRIVE SAVE THE CUPS Behind the dollars raised are women navigating diagnoses, treatment and circumstances that extend far beyond cancer itself. Kendra Levering, Missouri Kendra Levering’s breast cancer diagnosis turned her life upside down, forcing her to navigate chemotherapy, fertility preservation and the uncertainty that came with treatment. Throughout it all, small routines helped her hold onto a sense of normalcy — including regular trips to Swig, sometimes even while wearing her cold cap during treatment. Kendra was selected as a Save The Cups recipient in 2025, bringing her connection to Swig full circle and providing meaningful financial support during one of the most difficult chapters of her life. Carrie McKee, Utah For Carrie McKee, Save The Cups played a role before she even knew she had breast cancer. Carrie visited Swig’s Oquirrh Mountain location in Utah and made a donation to Save The Cups. That simple moment prompted her to think about her own health, and she realized she was overdue for a mammogram. She scheduled the appointment. That mammogram led to her breast cancer diagnosis. Carrie’s story has become a powerful reminder of why early detection is an important part of the Save The Cups mission. The campaign was created to ease the financial burden for women fighting breast cancer, and Swig also hopes it encourages women to schedule the appointment, get checked and prioritize their own health. Joy Skarka, Florida Joy Skarka was 32 years old when she discovered a lump in March 2025 while at the hospital with her husband, who was battling brain cancer. Months later, Joy underwent a double mastectomy, just 10 days before her husband passed away in August 2025. Suddenly, Joy was navigating her own breast cancer treatment while grieving the loss of her husband and caring for their two young children. When the Save The Cups team arrived at Joy’s home to surprise her with the news that she had been selected to receive support, Joy shared that it was the couple’s first home, the place where they had brought their children home and built their life together. Stories like Kendra’s, Carrie’s and Joy’s are why Save The Cups continues to grow. While every woman’s circumstances are different, the goal remains the same: ease the financial burden during a time when families are already carrying more than enough. HOW TO GET INVOLVED Now through October 10, proceeds from Swig’s fall menu and merchandise will support Save The Cups. Customers can also contribute by rounding up their purchase at participating Swig locations. Save The Cups is also accepting nominations for women currently fighting breast cancer. To learn more about Save The Cups, nominate a loved one for assistance or apply for yourself, visit SaveTheCups.org . articles.title: Whit’s Frozen Custard Opening in Lexington, South Carolina
articles.titleKo: Whit’s Frozen Custard Opening in Lexington, South Carolina
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Whit’s Frozen Custard is officially open in Lexington, bringing its fresh-made frozen custard and welcoming, neighborhood atmosphere to The Shoppes at White Knoll at 1788 South Lake Drive, Suite 170. To celebrate the new Lexington business, the Lexington Chamber of Commerce will conduct an official ribbon-cutting ceremony at the store on Wednesday, September 16, at 11:30 a.m. The new location, which opened September 4, is locally owned and operated by Jay and Lori Pearson, who are both actively involved in the business and share a vision of making Whit’s Frozen Custard of Lexington more than simply a place to stop for dessert. “We’ve spent a tremendous amount of time bringing this store to life and seeing customers finally walk through the doors has made all of that work worthwhile,” said Jay Pearson. “Our goal is for Whit’s to become a place where families, friends, neighbors, sports teams and community groups can come together, enjoy something great and feel genuinely welcome.” For the Pearsons, the decision to bring Whit’s to Lexington grew from an appreciation for the brand’s product quality, family-friendly atmosphere and emphasis on locally owned stores that become part of the communities they serve. “We want people to walk through our doors and immediately feel comfortable and welcomed,” said Lori Pearson. “We’re excited to get to know our customers, build relationships throughout Lexington and create a place people look forward to visiting again and again.” Whit’s Frozen Custard is known for frozen custard made fresh in the store, with vanilla and chocolate available alongside rotating Flavor of the Day and Flavor of the Week selections. Guests can enjoy traditional scoops as well as signature Whitsers, Whitties, shakes, sundaes, floats and other frozen treats. The Lexington location also offers frozen custard cakes, take-home options and catering for events and gatherings. “Jay and Lori embody the kind of local ownership that makes Whit’s special,” said Bill Aseere, CEO of Whit’s Frozen Custard. “They’re not just opening a store in Lexington—they’re putting their time, energy and personalities into creating a place where people will feel at home. We’re excited to welcome them to the Whit’s family and know they’re going to make a wonderful addition to the Lexington community.” Community involvement will be an important part of the Lexington store’s mission. The Pearsons plan to build partnerships with area schools, youth sports organizations, nonprofits and other local groups throughfundraisers, events, sponsorships and other opportunities to give back. “We live here, and we want Whit’s to be part of the community we call home,” Jay Pearson said. “Opening the doors was really just the beginning. We’re looking forward to building relationships with our customers and with organizations throughout Lexington for many years to come.” The Wednesday ribbon cutting at 11:30 a.m. will mark another milestone for the new business and provide an opportunity to celebrate Whit’s arrival in the Lexington community alongside representatives of the Lexington Chamber of Commerce. articles.title: Chipotle Bolsters Apprentice Program to Focus on Talent Development
articles.titleKo: Chipotle Bolsters Apprentice Program to Focus on Talent Development
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Today, Apprentices support approximately three-quarters of Chipotle's restaurants. Chipotle Mexican Grill announced enhancements to its Apprentice program that place greater emphasis on developing talent, strengthening restaurant operations and preparing leaders to support the company’s continued growth. As the company works toward its long-term goal of operating 7,000 restaurants across the U.S. and Canada, it expects to open between 350 and 370 new restaurants in 2026. To enable its expansion, the company aims to place an Apprentice in each of its more than 4,200 company-owned restaurants by the end of 2027, strengthening the management infrastructure needed to support its growing footprint. Today, Apprentices support approximately three-quarters of Chipotle’s restaurants. Extending the model across its entire restaurant portfolio will create additional opportunities for Crew Members to advance while building deeper management benches across the organization. More than 85 percent of Chipotle’s restaurant managers began their careers as Crew Members, underscoring the company’s commitment to promoting from within. The Apprentice role serves as a critical bridge to becoming a General Manager, preparing high-performing employees to oversee restaurant operations, develop teams and uphold Chipotle’s operational standards. Chipotle’s career pathway provides employees with a clear roadmap to advance from Crew Member to General Manager-and ultimately into field and regional roles. “Every Crew Member we hire has the potential to become a future restaurant leader,” said Ilene Eskenazi, Chief Legal and Human Resources Officer. “Developing leaders from within allows us to create meaningful careers for our people while ensuring every restaurant is led by someone who understands our culture and our commitment to exceptional guest experiences.” In addition to building Chipotle’s pipeline of future General Managers, Apprentices provide additional leadership and staffing coverage during peak periods and weekends, helping teams focus on operational execution. The role also helps build a stronger team culture while delivering more consistent guest experiences across in-restaurant and digital occasions. By taking ownership of key areas, including training and the digital makeline, Apprentices allow General Managers to distribute responsibilities more effectively, improve digital execution and consistently deliver Chipotle’s standards for hospitality. Restaurants with Apprentices also generally achieve better operational scores, which can contribute to improved restaurant economics over the long term. Building Leaders Through Education This year marks the 10th anniversary of Cultivate Education, powered by Guild, a leading education and upskilling company. Over the past decade, the program has become a cornerstone of Chipotle’s leadership strategy, helping employees gain the education, skills and confidence to advance their careers. Key Cultivate Education milestones over the past decade include: Nearly 25,000 Chipotle employees have enrolled in an education program More than 14,000 employees have completed an education program 57 percent of graduates earned a college degree, while 43 percent earned a certificate Eligible Chipotle employees can pursue fully online bachelor’s and associate degrees, certificates, boot camps, language learning, high school completion and college preparation programs. Chipotle pays 100 percent of tuition for select college degree programs and provides up to $5,250 annually toward additional educational opportunities or tuition reimbursement. Employees also receive one-on-one coaching throughout their educational journey and can earn college credit for eligible on-the-job training through Guild. Brady will lead Jamba's strategy and operations, partnering closely with franchisees and restaurant teams to strengthen the core business, deepen guest relevance and unlock new avenues for sustainable growth. GoTo Foods, parent company of Auntie Anne’s, Carvel, Cinnabon, Jamba, McAlister’s Deli, Moe’s Southwest Grill and Schlotzsky’s Deli, announced the appointment of Lucy Brady as President of Jamba, along with expanded leadership roles across several other brands and core business functions. The leadership appointments include: Lucy Brady , who joined GoTo Foods as President of Jamba on September 8. Nathan Baldwin , President of Auntie Anne’s , who is expanding his role to President of Specialty Brands , now also overseeing Cinnabon, Carvel and Co-Brands . Francisco Bram , Chief Growth Officer , who has also been named President of Moe’s Southwest Grill . Biplav Misra , who has been named Chief Digital & Technology Officer , formally adding Technology to his existing oversight of Digital. “These appointments come at an important time for GoTo Foods as we reinforce our commitment to best serve our customers and partner closely with our franchisees across the portfolio,” said Omer Gajial, Chief Executive Officer of GoTo Foods. “Strengthening our leadership structure will create greater organizational agility and allow us to remain focused on what matters most: growing category-leading brands, supporting franchisee success, and delivering experiences that keep guests coming back.” Lucy Brady Named President of Jamba Brady will lead Jamba’s strategy and operations, partnering closely with franchisees and restaurant teams to strengthen the core business, deepen guest relevance and unlock new avenues for sustainable growth. She brings extensive experience leading and transforming large consumer businesses, most recently as President of Grocery & Snacks at Conagra Brands, where she led a $5 billion portfolio of more than 60 brands. Earlier in her career at McDonald’s, Brady held senior leadership roles spanning strategy, innovation, and digital customer experience, where she played a key role in the company’s transformation and helped build major growth platforms including MyMcDonald’s Rewards, McDelivery and digital ordering. “Jamba is one of those rare brands that is instantly recognizable,” Brady said. “I am excited to work alongside our brand, franchisee and restaurant teams to make Jamba even more relevant to today’s guests, expand the occasions we serve and deliver an exceptional experience every time.” Nathan Baldwin Appointed President of Specialty Brands Baldwin, who has been leading the Auntie Anne’s brand since he joined GoTo Foods in 2025, has been named President of Specialty Brands and will be assuming responsibility for Cinnabon, Carvel and GoTo Foods’ Co-Brands strategy. Drawing on more than 25 years of restaurant industry experience, his expanded role brings together brands with complementary operating models, physical footprints and development opportunities, in order to create greater potential to delight guests and improve franchisee profitability. Francisco Bram Named President of Moe’s Southwest Grill Bram will lead Moe’s Southwest Grill while continuing to serve as Chief Growth Officer of GoTo Foods, overseeing enterprise growth functions that include loyalty, marketing, consumer research, analytics, PR and social media. A central priority will be advancing the ongoing reimagination of Moe’s brand positioning and how that comes to life for the guest through menu and restaurant experience, plus the broader franchisee growth strategy. Bram brings more than 17 years of experience in brand strategy, digital marketing and customer growth to the Moe’s brand, including previous leadership roles at Chewy, Albertsons Companies, Uber and Siemens. articles.title: Former KFC Global CEO Sabir Sami Joins Chipotle’s Board
articles.titleKo: Former KFC Global CEO Sabir Sami Joins Chipotle’s Board
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chipotle Mexican Grill announced a new addition to its board of directors, Sabir Sami, effective immediately. Sabir Sami brings more than 30 years of global consumer and restaurant industry experience, including 16 years at Yum! Brands Inc., where he held a series of senior leadership roles across KFC, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill. Most recently, Mr. Sami served as chief executive officer of KFC from January 2022 to February 2025, with global responsibility for the brand’s strategy and performance and reporting directly to the chief executive officer of Yum! Brands. Previously, he served as KFC’s chief operating officer and managing director of KFC Asia, leading the brand’s global operations team while overseeing markets across Thailand, India, Central Asia and Greater Asia. Mr. Sami also served as managing director of KFC’s Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan and Turkey markets. During his tenure at Yum! Brands, he held leadership roles across all three of the company’s brands, including serving as general manager of Yum! Canada and in general manager roles for KFC’s Canada and Turkey businesses. Before joining Yum! Brands in 2009, Mr. Sami held various leadership roles at Procter & Gamble, The Coca-Cola Co. and Reckitt Benckiser. In addition to his role at Chipotle, Mr. Sami serves as a director of Sami Advisory, a business consulting firm he founded in August 2025. He also serves on the Board of Directors of Save the Children Canada. Mr. Sami holds an MBA from the University of Karachi in Pakistan. “I’m thrilled to join Chipotle’s Board at such an exciting time for the company. With an iconic brand and global fanfare, Chipotle has an immense opportunity to bring its craveable menu to more guests around the world. I look forward to helping the company realize its significant potential.” With the change announced today, Chipotle’s Board of Directors will be composed of 11 directors, 10 of whom are independent. Mr. Sami brings significant global restaurant industry and operational expertise to the board. The board remains committed to ongoing refreshment and will continue to evaluate highly qualified independent director candidates who bring relevant experience and perspectives aligned with Chipotle’s long-term strategy. “Sabir brings deep restaurant operating expertise and a proven track record leading brands across international markets,” said Scott Maw, Chairman. “That experience will be invaluable as we scale Chipotle with intention, strengthen our operations and expand access to our brand around the world.” The post Former KFC Global CEO Sabir Sami Joins Chipotle’s Board appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: LeBron James Invests in Growth-Ready Mike’s Red Tacos
articles.titleKo: LeBron James Invests in Growth-Ready Mike’s Red Tacos
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mike's Red Tacos built its leadership team for scale. LeBron James is no stranger to restaurant deals. Especially when they involve this leadership team. The sports icon Tuesday announced he’s joining Mike’s Red Tacos as an investor. Terms were not disclosed. The fast casual, which claims more than 300 franchise locations in development nationwide, is chaired by Bill Phelps, who cofounded Wetzel’s Pretzels in 1994 and later became a founding investor in Blaze Pizza, which James, business partner Maverick Carter, and financial adviser Paul Wachter of Main Street Advisors, got behind for less than $1 million in 2012 when the brand had about 10 locations. Phelps in 2019 then joined Dave’s Hot Chicken as investor and CEO (a position today held by Jim Bitticks). James and Main Street Advisors hold a stake in that rising brand, too, which ended 2025 with 358 restaurants and was sold last June to Roark Capital for $1 billion . A release Monday explained James and Main Street Advisors felt comfortable with the Mike’s Red Tacos management team and “had conviction in the company’s vision and long-term growth strategy and were excited to invest and help bring Mike’s Red Tacos to more communities across the country.” Mike’s Red Tacos in August appointed Andrew Feghali—the first Dave’s Hot Chicken franchisee—as CEO, with founder Mike Touma taking on the role of chief brand officer. Feghali became involved with Mike’s Red Tacos as an early investor and board member alongside Phelps and their firm Four Wall Partners. The fast casual at the time also announced Stephen Jennings, formerly of Marie Callendar’s and Ruby’s Diner, as CFO, Vincent Montanelli as COO (he was president), and Patrick Cunningham as CDO. They brought over experience from Wetzel’s, Dunkin’, Baskin-Robbins, Little Caesars, and Bobby’s Burgers by Bobby Flay. Additionally, Nate Zelazoski, with stops at Five Guys and Smashburger, was tapped VP of real estate, and Blaze Pizza, Taco Bell, and Pizza Hut leader Lance Salsman joined as SVP of operations. “I love tacos, and I especially love how they bring people together to create traditions and share great moments around the table with family and friends. In addition to having an incredible taco, Mike’s Red Tacos brings those same values to life in a fresh, new way for consumers,” James said in a statement. “With this leadership team, I see a group that is building something authentic with a long-term vision, and I wanted to be part of helping bring that experience to more communities.” Mike’s Red Tacos started as a San Diego food truck in 2021. Touma grew it to two San Diego locations (the first brick-and-mortar debuted in August 2022) serving beef birria tacos, featuring slow-braised meat served with a rich consommé for dipping. The menu showcases burritos, loaded nachos and fries, and birria ramen as well. Feghali and Phelps got involved in February as Mike’s Red Tacos kicked off a franchising push. Phelps says he visited one store and observed wide appeal, just as he did with Dave’s. According to Datassential, birria now appears on about 4 percent of menus nationwide, more than quadrupling over a four-year span. As he has throughout his career, though, Phelps didn’t view the opportunity as chasing a trend. He felt Mike’s Red Tacos could build a focused brand within a larger category. “There’s tons of competition, but we believe that birria tacos are a great niche within the Mexican food space in the same way that hot chicken is a great niche within the chicken space,” Phelps previously told QSR . “We think we can carve out that niche and hopefully be the leader in that niche.” Feghali, also one of the country’s largest Little Caesars operators, created Four Wall Partners with Phelps to advise emerging restaurant brands with franchising potential. articles.title: Workplace Violence is a Big Issue in QSR. Here’s How to Start Countering It
articles.titleKo: Workplace Violence is a Big Issue in QSR. Here’s How to Start Countering It
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . There’s a price to be paid for such an environment by individual workers, but by the organization itself. An employee at a Greensboro, North Caroliona, McDonald’s was physically attacked in June by a group of juvenile girls. They were fighting among themselves in the restaurant and turned on her when she asked them to leave. In January, a routine refund dispute sparked explicit death threats by an aggressive customer against a crew of Paul’s Drive In in Kansas City. In another recent incident, after receiving an order they said was wrong, two customers of LJK Round 2 in Baton Rouge left, then came back with a gun, leaving the owner hospitalized for weeks. Violence against restaurant workers, particularly in quick and fast serve establishments, is rampant. Yet, it doesn’t usually start with a weapon. It takes other forms, at least initially: threats, verbal abuse, bullying, humiliation and degrading language or behavior directed at employees. It may or may not escalate to physical violence. While the risk in the QSR sector trails certain other business sectors—think law enforcement and healthcare—violence is still alarmingly prevalent. Nearly 65 percent of restaurant employees overall are exposed at some point in their careers. It’s usually meted out by customers, brought on late at night by aggressiveness or drunkenness or disputes over order accuracy and pricing. Vulnerabilities are heightened by workplace designs and service protocols. There’s a price to be paid for such an environment by individual workers, but by the organization itself. A hostile work environment erodes wellbeing, morale, retention and performance. It reflects disengagement that can drag down profitability by as much as 23 percent. Accepting abuse as a condition of employment is not acceptable. An effective prevention program that recognizes and responds to early warning signs of such a toxic environment, is essential. It shows an employer is taking seriously what employees experience every day. The same systematic approach used for any workplace hazard will help construct a solid framework for the program. Here are the steps to take. Enlist leadership support. Credibility and momentum are best accomplished when your leadership views prevention as a top priority and treats it accordingly. Evaluate risks specific to the business. Every QSR establishment has a different risk profile. Employees may work alone in isolated areas. Alcohol service can up the exposure. Cash transactions pose another issue. Hosting large events is a risk as well. Identifying each factor that represents an exposure is key for shaping necessary controls. Establish clear policies and reporting channels. A written prevention policy covers threat assessment protocols, security measures and emergency procedures. Employees must have a simple and reliable way to report concerns, like a dedicated phone line, email address or clear reporting chain. If the process is complicated, people won’t use it. Training and empowerment count. Not only should employee be equipped to recognize escalation warning signs, but they need to know exactly how to report concerns. Build a threat assessment capability. One or two people must be assigned responsibility for evaluating and responding to reports. Also important are structured assessment tools that remove the subjectivity that leads to uneven responses. By assessing vulnerabilities and implementing effective policies, organizations will create a safer environment where their teams—and business will thrive. articles.title: Why Florida is Leading America’s Burger Boom
articles.titleKo: Why Florida is Leading America’s Burger Boom
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . White Castle returned to Florida in 2021 with its Orlando flagship location. For decades, Florida has served as a proving ground for restaurant brands. If a concept can succeed here, it often has the foundation to expand almost anywhere. That dynamic hasn’t changed. If anything, that trend has become even more pronounced in recent years. One of the clearest examples is the resurgence of the burger. From century-old brands entering new markets to fast-growing regional smash burger concepts, restaurant operators are actively looking for space across Florida and competing for prime locations that can give them the best shot at long-term success. The strategies may vary from brand to brand, but the fundamentals are largely the same: Florida continues to attract new residents, millions of visitors each year and consumers who are still looking for convenient, familiar and affordable dining options. Florida Offers Scale Few States Can Match There are two reasons Florida continues to attract restaurant investment. First, people continue to move here. Florida, alongside Texas, remains one of the country’s fastest-growing states. Unlike many markets, however, that growth isn’t concentrated in one metropolitan area. From Miami and Orlando, to Tampa and Jacksonville, Florida, offers multiple large, diverse markets allowing brands to establish regional scale without leaving the state. For restaurant operators, that’s incredibly attractive. Rather than learning several different markets, brands can build a Florida strategy that reaches millions of consumers across multiple metropolitan areas with similar demographic tailwinds. At the same time, Florida remains the country’s premier tourism destination according to VISIT Florida, welcoming over 143.3 million visitors in 2025 . Millions of visitors arrive every year already familiar with brands they know and trust. Others discover new concepts while vacationing and become customers long after returning home. That creates an unusually powerful combination of local demand and built-in brand awareness that few other states can replicate. From Legacy Brands to Local Favorites The current burger boom taking over the Sunshine State is not a trend fueled by a single type of restaurant. Legacy brands are still able to expand throughout the country proving that decades of consumer loyalty still matter. White Castle, for example, returned to Florida in 2021 with its Orlando flagship location after years of consumer demand that was fueled, in part, by a grassroots social media campaign asking the company to return to the state. At the same time, newer concepts are finding their footing by bringing something different to the table, whether that’s a unique take on the burger, a fresh brand identity or a strong connection with customers online. Florida-based Skinny Louie’s is a good example. The local concept has built a loyal following through its food, personality and social media presence, creating a digital momentum that can help support expansion into new markets. National brands are active, too. Shake Shack, Five Guys and other growing concepts continue to add locations across Florida, creating even more competition for the best sites. For consumers, that means more choices than ever. But there’s a reason burgers continue to have such staying power: they’re familiar, relatively affordable and appeal to a wide range of customers from children to seniors. In a market where people are paying closer attention to what they spend on dining out, that broad appeal matters. Real Estate Strategy Is Evolving with the Customer Base The way restaurant brands think about real estate has changed, too. articles.title: Why IHOP Finally Brought Back Stuffed French Toast
articles.titleKo: Why IHOP Finally Brought Back Stuffed French Toast
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . For six years, IHOP guests kept asking the same question. When is Stuffed French Toast coming back? The requests showed up on social media and in restaurants. They came from customers and employees. Lawrence Kim heard them firsthand after becoming IHOP president and visiting more than 150 restaurants over two years. IHOP finally has an answer. Stuffed French Toast returned nationwide September 14, reviving a product that first debuted in 2003 and eventually earned a permanent menu spot before disappearing six years ago. This time, IHOP is giving it more prominence, introducing Stuffed French Toast as its own menu category with Strawberry Vanilla and Blueberry Vanilla varieties. The launch is rooted in a simple idea. IHOP saw an opportunity to give customers something they had spent years requesting. “Some people may think that bringing back and relaunching Stuffed French Toast is random, but we all know it is not random,” Kim says. “… Every time I speak with guests, every time I speak even with our cooks, they ask me, ‘Can you please bring back Stuffed French Toast?’” IHOP did not simply pull the old recipe from storage. The company reviewed historical customer comments and the original product specifications to determine what people loved and what could be improved. The overwhelming response was that guests wanted the product they remembered. One recurring request offered IHOP an opening. Customers wanted more sweet cream. Kim challenged the culinary team to increase the filling without compromising the French toast itself. IHOP tested roughly 100 versions, and a supplier developed a proprietary injection process that distributes more cream through the bread. “It’s filled from corner to corner,” Kim says. “So when you cut into that Stuffed French Toast, you just get that bite of sweet cream with practically every bite.” Each order features two triangles filled with sweet cream, dipped and griddled in IHOP’s vanilla-cinnamon French toast batter. Guests can choose glazed strawberries or blueberry topping with vanilla sauce. The comeback builds on years of work around IHOP’s French toast lineup. The chain introduced Thick ’N Fluffy French Toast in 2022 and refreshed the full platform in 2024. Stuffed French Toast gives the company another signature breakfast item at a point when its core category continues to carry significant weight across the menu. More than 75 percent of IHOP orders are breakfast items regardless of daypart, according to the company. That creates room for products that can function as indulgent standalone orders or become part of larger breakfast combinations with eggs, bacon, and other staples. The launch also arrives after IHOP spent much of the past year and a half building its everyday value platform. Kim says that strategy helped the chain outperform Black Box category traffic trends for six consecutive quarters. Stuffed French Toast gives IHOP another lever. Instead of relying solely on value to create visits, the chain can use a recognizable premium breakfast product to give customers another reason to come in. “When you come to IHOP, and we are really tied to our breakfast equities, we’re really driving that combo nature because it’s what people crave,” Kim says. “That eggs, the bacon—it’s just a perfect complement to that of something like the Stuffed French Toast.” Determining which products deserve menu space requires IHOP to balance customer requests with timing. The company maintains what Kim calls its “pantry,” a collection of hundreds of products that have been ideated and developed. Some eventually reach restaurants. Others stay on the shelf until consumer behavior or cultural trends create an opening. That means a popular retired item does not automatically qualify for a comeback. articles.originalSummary: The future of Café Pacifico in Covent Garden is uncertain following the appointment of liquidators to its operating company. Robert Dymond and Joanne Hammond of Begbies Traynor were appointed joint liquidators of Laverlathe Limited last month. Laverlathe, which continues to be named as Café Pacifico’s operator on the restaurant’s website, was compulsorily wound up in March following a petition filed last November. The restaurant, which claims to be London’s oldest Mexican restaurant, remains open and continues to take bookings.

articles.title: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.titleKo: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.originalSummary: Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy is expanding beyond her seven-strong London restaurant portfolio and existing French Riviera hotel, with a new hotel development and art-led villa on the Mediterranean coast. The businesswoman behind the Wild Group, the eight-figure hospitality group that includes some of London’s most coveted restaurants, including Belvedere, Wild Tavern, Wild Izakaya, Wild Corner, Wild Notting Hill, Chelsea Grill and Pinna Mayfair, has revealed the next stage of her wider hospitality portfolio, with two major projects underway on the French Riviera. Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy, formerly of Barclays Capital, Nomura and UBS , is preparing to restore and redevelop a collection of historic buildings into a new hotel, named Hotel Les Chardons, while also creating a private seven-bedroom art villa at her existing luxury hotel, Hostellerie La Farandole. The villa is being created in partnership with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano, who is designing the property in its entirety, from its recycled materials and interiors to original stone sculptures, creating a villa that will be a work of art in its own right . Meanwhile, plans for Hotel Les Chardons are taking shape , with Amdiy currently developing the concept around a potential focus on wellness and longevity . The historic buildings will be carefully restored and redeveloped, with architectural plans revealing landscaped gardens, restaurant terraces overlooking the French Riviera and a large outdoor swimming pool with an expansive poolside lounge area. Amdiy said: “Hotel Les Chardons is a significant project for us. We’re taking a collection of existing buildings and creating something new around them, while also being very conscious of what is already there and what we can restore. If we do take Les Chardons in the wellness and longevity direction, we will make sure there is real substance behind it, and a reason for people to travel specifically to stay with us. ” The projects mark a significant expansion of Amdiy’s hospitality interests beyond London, where she has spent the past five years working alongside her partners and team to build Wild Group from a single restaurant into a £20m+ portfolio spanning seven venues and employing more than 300 Londoners . Her involvement in hospitality began in France. Alongside her career in investment banking, Amdiy was already involved in the ownership of Hostellerie La Farandole before investing in Wild Tavern in 2020 and going on to help build the wider Wild Group portfolio. A SEVEN-BEDROOM VILLA CREATED AS A WORK OF ART The seven-bedroom private villa at Hostellerie La Farandole is on track for completion by the end of 2026, when it will become available to book through the hotel. Set within private grounds, the villa will have its own swimming pool and pétanque area . Amdiy is working closely with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano on the design of the entire villa , with art and design being developed together from the outset. His involvement spans materials, furniture and lighting to original sculptures created specifically for the property and its grounds . Amdiy said : “I didn’t want us to design the villa and then decide what art to put on the walls afterwards. Grishi has been involved from the very beginning, so the art is part of the design rather than something added at the end. We have quite different instincts, which is what makes the collaboration interesting. My taste is far more classical, while Grishi will push things much further. We challenge each other, and that’s often how we get to the best result.” Giano said: “My role goes far beyond creating the artworks. articles.title: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.titleKo: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.originalSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date. Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience. Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed. Central patios, generous proportions, fountains, handcrafted materials and lush greenery give the space its structure and soul, evoking the kind of environment that takes decades to settle into its surroundings. Antique furniture sits alongside bespoke pieces, and reclaimed terracotta, natural stone, marble and aged timber are used throughout, materials that carry history and wear it well. “People rarely talk about specific design features. They talk about the atmosphere,” adds Alexis. “If people leave believing the space possesses a history, then we have succeeded in creating something that feels authentic rather than constructed.” A considered selection of suppliers and craftspeople underpins the interior. Sogni and Pooky provide the lighting, Pierre Frey and Morris the fabrics and upholstery, and Mandarin Stone the marble and stone surfaces. Flexhouse – responsible for custom joinery, millwork and bespoke fabrication – also contributed to the furniture alongside vintage pieces and Leta, while Resources delivered the decorative wall finishes. Together they bring a layered quality to the space, as though each element has its own provenance and story. With its new 280-cover restaurant, hacienda-inspired interiors and striking luminescent bar stocked with more than 2700 bottles, Tigermilk Spitalfields invites guests into what feels like the brand’s thirteenth home. Through a considered interior scheme full of texture and attention to detail, the restaurant offers a transportive South American-inspired experience designed to engage every sense.
koreanSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date.

Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience.
Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed.
